description: A VIBRANT KALEIDOSCOPE OF SUN-KISSED PEPPERS AND FLUFFY BASMATI TOPPED WITH THE SILKY LUXURY OF A PERFECT EGG.

instructions.text: Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Sauté the vibrant bell peppers for about 4-5 minutes until they become tender and aromatic, but ensure they do not brown too much to avoid any bitterness.

Gently fold the rinsed rice into the peppers, stirring for 2 minutes to coat every grain in the fragrant oil. For a 'Royal Upgrade,' drizzle your bloomed saffron over the rice now to impart a celestial golden hue.

Pour in 3 cups of water (or follow the 1.5:1 water-to-rice ratio), adding the sea salt and red pepper flakes. Bring the pot to a vigorous boil over medium-high heat until the water level drops to the surface of the rice.
Reduce the heat to the lowest setting, wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap the steam, and let the rice infuse and fluff for 25-30 minutes until perfectly tender.

While the rice rests, fry the eggs in a separate pan until the whites are crispy and lacy at the edges but the yolks remain rich and runny. Serve the rice in a heap with the golden eggs perched elegantly on top.

english_name: Royal Golden Rice with Fava Beans (Dampokhtak)
description: A VIBRANT, BUTTERY SYMPHONY OF TURMERIC-INFUSED RICE AND MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH YELLOW BEANS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water several times until the starch is removed and the water runs crystal clear. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes to ensure elongated, fluffy grains.
In a small pot, bring the yellow fava beans to a gentle boil with a pinch of salt. Simmer for about 10 minutes until they are tender to the bite but still hold their shape. Drain and set aside.
In your main non-stick pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Sauté the grated onion until it becomes translucent. Stir in the turmeric, allowing its earthy aroma to bloom and color the oil a deep gold.

Add the drained rice and parboiled beans to the pot with the onions. Pour in enough water to cover the rice by about half an inch (the 'finger-joint' rule). Add the butter and salt. Bring to a rapid boil until most of the liquid is absorbed and small steam holes appear on the surface.

Drizzle the liquid saffron over the rice for the 'Royal Upgrade.' Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to seal in the steam. Reduce heat to the lowest setting and let the rice steam undisturbed for 35 minutes to develop a perfect golden crust.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald Rice (Nokhod Farangi Polo)
description: A VIBRANT SYMPHONY OF SWEET PEAS AND WARM SPICES NESTLED IN CLOUDS OF FLUFFY BASMATI.

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash the Basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for 45 minutes to achieve the signature long, fluffy Persian grain.
In a large pan, sauté the grated onions with turmeric in oil over medium heat until they become translucent and develop a beautiful golden hue.
Add the minced garlic to the onions, stirring constantly for about a minute until the aroma is released without browning the garlic.
Stir in the grated carrot, whole peppercorns, and ground cardamom. Sauté for 5 minutes until the carrot is tender and the spices are toasted.
Fold the green peas into the aromatic base, mixing gently to coat every pea in the golden spice oil.
Sprinkle the ground cinnamon over the mixture, stir once, and immediately remove from heat to keep the cinnamon's fragrance bright and sharp.

Boil the soaked rice in a large pot of salted water until 'al dente' (soft on the outside, firm in the middle), drain, then layer the rice and pea mixture in a pot. For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle bloomed saffron over the top layer.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel, place it firmly on the pot, and steam on low heat until the rice is perfectly fluffy and a crispy Tahdig crust forms at the bottom.

english_name: Royal Persian Tomato & Lamb Rice (Istanbul Polo)
description: THE ULTIMATE COMFORT BOWL WHERE RUBY-RED RICE MEETS MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH LAMB.

instructions.text: Place the lamb cubes in a heavy pot with two cups of water. Bring to a gentle boil, skim any impurities from the surface, then cover and simmer for 60-70 minutes until the meat is fork-tender. Strain the meat and reserve the rich lamb broth.
In a large non-stick pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Sauté the minced onion for 8-10 minutes until it reaches a beautiful, shimmering translucent gold, releasing its natural sweetness.
Incorporate the cubed potatoes, bell pepper, and the cooked lamb into the onions. Sauté for 7 minutes, stirring frequently, until the potatoes begin to brown at the edges and the flavors meld.
Create a well in the center of the pot and add the tomato paste. Sizzle it in the butter for 2 minutes—this 'blooming' technique is essential to develop a deep ruby color and complex, savory depth.

Fold in the washed rice, ensuring every grain is coated in the tomato-butter essence. Pour in the reserved lamb broth plus two cups of boiling water. Season generously with salt and pepper to elevate the aromatic profile.

Cook on medium-high until the water is mostly absorbed and small craters form on the rice surface. If using, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel, seal tightly, and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to achieve the legendary golden bottom crust.

english_name: Persian Shooshtari Dill & Chicken Rice
description: A FRAGRANT TAPESTRY OF FRESH DILL AND TENDER CHICKEN FROM THE HISTORIC HEART OF KHUZESTAN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch clears. Soak in heavily salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the grains achieve maximum length and elegance.
In a large skillet, sauté the golden fried onions with the chicken morsels. Season with turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Sear until the chicken is golden and sizzling.
Pour in a small cup of water and half of your bloomed saffron. Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the chicken is succulent and the liquid has reduced to a rich, fragrant glaze.
Gently fold the cooked black-eyed peas and the fresh chopped dill into the chicken mixture. Let the flavors marry for 2 minutes, then remove from heat.
Parboil the soaked rice in boiling water until the exterior is soft but the core remains 'al dente'. Drain and rinse with cool water.
In a non-stick pot, drizzle oil and a splash of saffron water. Layer the rice and the chicken-herb mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Poke holes for steam to escape.
Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani). Steam over low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and a majestic golden crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.

english_name: Persian Aromatic Green Bean & Chicken Pilaf (Loobia Polo)
description: A SYMPHONY OF TENDER GREEN BEANS AND GOLDEN SAFFRON RICE THAT DEFINES PERSIAN COMFORT.

instructions.text: In a large skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat. Sauté the diced onions for 8 minutes until they turn a deep, translucent golden-brown.
Add the green beans to the onions and sauté for 6 minutes. You want them to soften slightly while retaining a vibrant green hue.
Incorporate the chicken fillets and seasonings into the pan. Sear for 5 minutes until the chicken is browned on all sides, releasing its savory juices.
Pour in 2 cups of filtered water. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the liquid has completely evaporated, leaving a thick, flavorful glaze.
The Royal Upgrade: Grind your saffron with a pinch of sugar and bloom it in 2 tablespoons of ice-cold water. Stir this golden elixir into the chicken and bean mixture.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, parboil the rice for 7 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a clean pot, add a layer of oil. Alternate layers of parboiled rice and the chicken-bean mixture, forming a pyramid shape. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel and steam on the lowest heat for 45 minutes until a crispy crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.

english_name: Royal Milk and Raisin Rice
description: INDULGE IN THE CREAMIEST ARISTOCRATIC RICE OF ANCIENT ARDABIL.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice gently in cold water multiple times until the water runs clear, ensuring all excess starch is removed for a fluffy finish.
In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, combine the whole milk, filtered water, and the rinsed rice. The milk provides a luxurious, creamy foundation for the grains.
Add sea salt and oil to the pot. Stir once gently. Set the heat to medium-low, bringing the mixture to a slow, controlled simmer. Do not leave it unattended, as milk can easily boil over.

Once the liquid has mostly absorbed and the rice is parboiled (tender on the outside but firm in the center), create a small well in the center and nestle the raisins on top. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle the liquid gold over one corner of the rice now.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Cover tightly and reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting. Steam for 35-40 minutes until a fragrant, golden crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.

english_name: Golden Silk Road Vegetable Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT TAPESTRY OF FLUFFY BASMATI AND GARDEN VEGETABLES KISSED BY THE ROYAL GLOW OF SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-10 minutes until the grains are 'Al Dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the center.

Drain the rice and set aside. In a small saucepan, combine the chicken stock, sweet corn, and diced carrots. Season with salt and pepper, and simmer over medium-low heat for 5 minutes to allow the vegetables to absorb the savory essence of the stock.
Stir the liquid gold—the bloomed saffron—into the vegetable and stock mixture. The aroma should be floral and heady. Remove from heat immediately to preserve the saffron's delicate volatile oils.
To serve with style, plate the fluffy white rice on a large platter. Reserve a small portion of rice to mix with the saffron-vegetable liquid, creating a vibrant yellow contrast.
Layer the saffron-infused rice and the colorful vegetables over the white rice. For the final touch, drizzle any remaining golden stock over the top for a glistening finish.

english_name: The Royal Persian Saffron Tahchin Crust
description: THE SHATTERINGLY CRISP, GOLDEN CROWN OF EVERY PERSIAN FEAST.

instructions.text: Parboil your Basmati rice in salted boiling water until 'Al Dente'—firm to the bite but not crunchy—then drain and let it cool slightly to stop the cooking process.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg and yogurt until completely smooth. Fold in the bloomed saffron, salt, and pepper until the mixture glows with a deep, royal amber hue.
Add approximately one-third of your parboiled rice to the saffron-yogurt mixture. Stir gently with a spatula to ensure every grain is coated in the aromatic gold.
Pour the vegetable oil into a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot. Tilt the pot to coat the bottom and the lower inch of the sides evenly.
Spread the saffron-rice mixture across the bottom of the pot, pressing down firmly with the back of a spoon to create a compacted, even layer. This is the secret to a 'glassy' shatter-crisp finish.

Gently layer the remaining white rice over the top. Cover with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel and steam over low-medium heat for 45 minutes until the edges are sizzling and deeply golden.

english_name: Royal Saffron & Eggplant Ribbon Tahchin
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CAKE OF FRAGRANT RICE, SUCCULENT CHICKEN, AND SILKY EGGPLANT.

instructions.text: In a pot, sauté the diced onion until translucent. Add the chicken breast, salt, and pepper with a splash of water. Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and fully cooked. Once cooled, shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Salt the eggplant rounds and let them sit for 15 minutes to sweat out any bitterness. Pat dry and fry in a pan with a little oil until golden-brown and soft. Set aside on a paper towel.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the washed Basmati rice and cook for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'al dente' (soft on the outside, firm in the center). Drain and rinse with cool water.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs, yogurt, and the royal saffron water until smooth. Gently fold the parboiled rice into this aromatic golden mixture until every grain is coated.
Grease a glass baking dish or heavy-bottomed non-stick pot with oil. Spread half of the saffron rice mixture as the base, pressing down slightly to compact it.

Layer the shredded chicken, barberries, and walnuts over the rice. Add a thin middle layer of rice, then arrange the golden eggplant rounds. Top with the remaining saffron rice and smooth the surface.
Drizzle the remaining vegetable oil over the top. Cover tightly with foil and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 60 minutes until the edges are visibly crispy and golden.
Allow the Tahchin to rest for 5 minutes before carefully inverting it onto a serving platter. Slice like a cake and serve immediately while the crust is at its peak crunch.

english_name: Persian Golden Cracked Wheat Pilaf (Dami Yarma)
description: A RUSTIC AZERBAIJANI TREASURE TRANSFORMED INTO A GOLDEN SYMPHONY OF WHOLE GRAINS AND CARAMELIZED VEGETABLES.

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Sauté the coarsely chopped onions until they reach a deep, translucent golden-amber hue, roughly 8-10 minutes.

Add the ground beef, turmeric, and tomato paste to the onions. Increase heat slightly and stir-fry for 5 minutes, ensuring the tomato paste 'blooms' in the oil to release its vibrant color and deep umami flavor.
Incorporate the diced carrots and potatoes. Reduce the flame to low, cover the pot tightly, and allow the vegetables to sweat and soften in the aromatic juices for 10 minutes.

Rinse the cracked wheat under cold water and add it to the pot. Pour in 2.5 cups of hot water and salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer uncovered until most of the liquid has been absorbed by the grains.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (damkoni). Place it back on the pot and steam on the lowest heat for 20 minutes. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle it over the top before the final 5 minutes of steaming.

english_name: Silk Road Spicy Chicken Kateh
description: A BOLD AND FRAGRANT ONE-POT MASTERPIECE FEATURING ZESTY VERJUICE AND WARM SILK ROAD SPICES.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot or non-stick caldron, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté the onions for 8-10 minutes until they achieve a deep, golden-brown caramelization.
Increase the heat slightly and add the chicken cubes. Sear the chicken until the edges are golden and the juices are locked in, about 5-6 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice and 3 cups of fresh water to the pot. Stir gently to combine the grains with the sautéed base.

Stir in the verjuice, butter, turmeric, curry, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. If using the saffron 'Royal Upgrade', pour it over the top now. The kitchen will begin to fill with an intoxicating, warm aroma.

Gently fold in the aromatic herbs. Bring the mixture to a brisk boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Allow the rice to simmer uncovered until most of the water has evaporated and small steam 'craters' appear on the surface.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (a traditional 'Damkani') to trap the steam. Cover tightly and reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting.
Allow the rice to steam slowly for 40 minutes. This creates the perfect fluffy texture and a delightful bottom crust (Tahdig). Fluff with a fork before serving.

english_name: Persian Chickpea & Spiced Meat Pilaf (Nokhod Polo)
description: A RUSTIC SILK ROAD MASTERPIECE FEATURING TENDER LAMB, EARTHY CHICKPEAS, AND THE MODERN CRISP OF ASPARAGUS.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the diced onions and sauté for about 8-10 minutes until they achieve a deep, translucent golden-brown hue.
Increase heat slightly and add the meat cubes. Sear the meat until all sides are browned and the juices are sealed in, creating a rich aromatic base.

Stir in the soaked chickpeas, cumin, cinnamon, black pepper, red pepper, and salt. Toast the spices for 1 minute until fragrant, then add 2 cups of hot water. Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the meat and chickpeas are tender.

Gently fold the washed rice into the pot. Ensure the liquid level is about half an inch above the rice; add a splash more hot water if necessary. Bring to a boil until the water mostly evaporates and small steam holes appear on the surface.
Arrange the thin asparagus pieces across the top of the rice. If using the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the center for a vivid golden crown.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Close tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes to develop a fluffy texture and a crisp bottom crust (Tahdig).

english_name: Persian Royal Layered Rice with Spiced Beef & Dill
description: A SYMPHONY OF FRAGRANT DILL AND GOLDEN SAFFRON CRUSTED RICE THAT DEFINES PERSIAN LUXURY.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water several times until the water runs clear to remove excess starch, ensuring fluffy grains.
In a large skillet, sauté the diced onion in oil over medium heat until it becomes translucent and takes on a deep golden-brown caramelization.

Add the ground meat to the onions. Brown the meat thoroughly, then stir in the curry powder, black pepper, garlic powder, and the diluted tomato paste. Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce reduces and coats the meat beautifully.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt and your bloomed 'Golden Touch' saffron. This will be the secret to your royal crust.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with 3 tablespoons of salt. Add the rice and par-boil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (Al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.
Mix 2 cups of the par-boiled rice with the saffron-yogurt mixture. Pour a generous layer of oil into the bottom of a non-stick pot and spread this golden mixture evenly to form the 'Tahdig' base.
Layer the remaining rice with the meat mixture, diced potatoes, and dill. Repeat the layers, shaping the rice into a pyramid. Drizzle lemon juice over the top.

Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel to trap steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 30 minutes until the rice is aromatic and fluffy.

english_name: Royal Persian Estamboli Polo (Tomato Rice with Succulent Lamb)
description: VIBRANT SCARLET BASMATI INFUSED WITH FRESH TOMATO ESSENCE AND TENDER MORSELS OF ROYAL LAMB.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water repeatedly until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. This ensures fluffy, separate grains.

Juice the fresh tomatoes. Combine the tomato juice with enough water to ensure the liquid level sits about two inches (two finger-joints) above the rice. Soak the rice in this vibrant liquid with 1 tablespoon of salt and 2 tablespoons of oil for at least 1 hour.

In a heavy-bottomed pan, sear the lamb cubes with the fried onions over medium-high heat until deep golden brown. Pour in 2 cups of boiling water, cover, and simmer gently for 45-60 minutes until the meat is fork-tender.
Once the lamb is tender and the liquid has mostly reduced, stir in the tomato paste, remaining salt, and pepper. Sauté for 3 minutes until the oil takes on a bright red hue and the aroma intensifies.

Place the soaking rice and its tomato liquid in a large pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Let it cook uncovered until the liquid has evaporated and small 'craters' form on the surface of the rice.

Create a well in the center of the rice and tuck the prepared lamb mixture inside. Cover the meat with the surrounding rice. If using the 'Golden Touch,' drizzle your bloomed saffron over a small corner of the rice now.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap steam. Steam on low heat for 45-50 minutes until the rice is fluffy and a crispy tomato crust (Tahdig) has formed at the bottom.

english_name: Royal Persian Tomato Rice with Crispy Potatoes
description: A SYMPHONY OF SUN-RIPENED TOMATOES, TENDER RICE, AND GOLDEN POTATO GEMS IN EVERY BITE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice repeatedly until the water runs crystal clear, then soak in salted water for at least 1 hour to ensure maximum grain length.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, sauté the onions in oil over medium heat until they reach a deep, translucent golden hue—the foundation of our flavor.
Add the ground meat to the onions, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon. Sizzle until browned and aromatic, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and tomato paste. Let them cook down until the tomatoes soften into a rustic, jammy sauce and the oil begins to separate.
In a separate pan, lightly fry the potato cubes until the edges are golden-crisp, then fold them into the meat and tomato mixture.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot along with the beef broth. Add extra water if needed until the liquid sits exactly one finger-width above the rice level.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. If choosing the 'Royal Upgrade,' drizzle your bloomed saffron over the top now for a floral, amber finish.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam perfectly. Simmer on the lowest heat for 45 minutes until a legendary golden crust forms at the bottom.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Aromatic Silk Road Emerald Rice
description: A VIBRANT JEWEL-TONED MASTERPIECE INFUSED WITH FRESH HERBS AND SILK ROAD SPICES.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch washes away and the water runs clear. In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the rice and toast gently for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until the grains are opaque and emit a nutty aroma.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a rolling boil. Immediately reduce the heat to the lowest setting to ensure a gentle simmer.

Carefully fold in the diced onion, green bell pepper, chili, and tomato. Do not over-mix; we want to maintain the integrity of the rice grains. Cover tightly and simmer for 12 minutes until the liquid is 90% absorbed.

Lift the lid and sprinkle the ground cumin, salt, and pepper over the rice. If you are opting for the Royal Upgrade, drizzle your golden bloomed saffron over one half of the rice for a stunning color contrast.

Scatter the minced garlic and fresh cilantro across the top. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (the 'Damkani' technique) to trap every drop of steam. Cover and let it steam on low heat for exactly 20 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the aromatics have infused every grain.

original_name: برنج با سبزیجات به روش چینی
english_name: Silk Road Aromatic Vegetable and Chicken Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT FUSION OF GARDEN-FRESH VEGETABLES AND TENDER CHICKEN WRAPPED IN A CLOUD OF STEAMED AROMATIC RICE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure maximum grain length.
In a large non-stick pot or wok, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat. Add the onions and sauté for 8-10 minutes until they reach a deep golden-brown caramelized state.
Add the chicken strips to the onions. Season with salt, pepper, turmeric, and curry powder. Sauté for 5 minutes until the chicken is seared and aromatic.
Incorporate the julienned carrots, zucchini, bell peppers, and potatoes. Toss frequently for 5 minutes, allowing the vegetables to soften slightly while retaining their vibrant color.
Cover the pot and let the mixture gently braise in its own juices for 5-7 minutes over low heat to meld the flavors.
In a separate pot of boiling salted water, parboil the soaked rice for 6-8 minutes until the exterior is soft but the core remains firm (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

Spread the chicken and vegetable mixture evenly at the bottom of a clean pot. Layer the parboiled rice gently on top, forming a pyramid shape. For a Royal Touch, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer of rice.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap steam. Cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and a golden crust forms at the bottom.

english_name: Persian Royal Raisin Rice with Tender Lamb Ribs
description: A LUXURIOUS SYMPHONY OF SUN-DRIED SWEETNESS AND FALL-OFF-THE-BONE LAMB INFUSED WITH ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a skillet over medium heat, sauté the diced onions in oil until they reach a deep golden-brown caramelization. Add the raisins and a pinch of turmeric, sautéing for just 2 minutes until they plump up beautifully.

Prepare the foundation: Pour 2 tablespoons of oil into a heavy-bottomed pot. Lay the bread pieces across the bottom to create a 'Tahdig' crust. Season the raw lamb ribs with salt and pepper and arrange them in a single layer directly on top of the bread.

Layering the aromatics: Spread one-third of the parboiled rice over the meat. Top with a layer of tomato slices, then sprinkle a portion of the cumin, garlic powder, sumac, and chili. Repeat the layers until the rice and spices are used.
The Golden Touch: Drizzle your bloomed saffron water over the top layer of rice in a circular motion. Spread the sautéed onion and raisin mixture evenly across the surface.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap steam. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat setting for 3.5 hours. This slow-braise allows the lamb juices to steam the rice while the meat becomes incredibly tender.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Royal Saffron Curry Pilaf
description: A GOLDEN SYMPHONY OF SILK ROAD SPICES AND FLUFFY SAFFRON GRAINS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch clears, then soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to achieve maximum grain length.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 7-10 minutes; drain when the grains are soft on the outside but still firm in the center.
In a large mixing bowl, delicately combine the shredded chicken, peas, sautéed mushrooms, one tablespoon of curry powder, and a drizzle of saffron water.
Coat the bottom of a heavy-bottomed pot with oil. Begin layering: start with a layer of rice, followed by the chicken-vegetable mixture, and a dusting of curry powder and saffron.
Continue layering until all ingredients are used, forming a pyramid shape with the rice to allow optimal steam circulation.
Whisk the remaining curry powder, saffron water, chicken broth, and melted butter together; pour this aromatic elixir evenly over the rice.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap steam. Cook on low heat for 50 minutes or bake at 350°F (175°C) until the rice is fluffy and aromatic.
Gently fluff the rice and transfer to a platter. Crown the dish with the crispy diced potatoes and pieces of golden Tahdig from the bottom of the pot.

english_name: Royal Persian Nesar Polo with Golden Saffron Chicken
description: A SYMPHONY OF SAFFRON, CITRUS, AND CRUNCHY JEWELS FIT FOR A PERSIAN EMPEROR.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in heavily salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a large skillet, melt 50g of butter over medium-high heat. Season the chicken fillets with salt and pepper, then sauté until they develop a beautiful golden-brown crust and are cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes.
Place the slivered almonds and pistachios in a small bowl with the rosewater. Let them macerate to absorb the floral essence and soften slightly.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Parboil for 6-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm snap in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

Melt 50g of butter in the bottom of a heavy-bottomed pot (non-stick is best for Tahdig). Layer one-third of the rice, followed by a sprinkle of cinnamon, some candied orange peels, and a portion of the soaked nuts. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used, shaping the rice into a pyramid.
Cover the pot lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Cook on low heat for 40 minutes to develop the crispy bottom crust and steam the grains to perfection.

In a small saucepan, melt the remaining butter and whisk in the orange peel syrup, bloomed saffron, and any remaining rosewater. Gently pour this golden elixir over the rice during the last 5 minutes of steaming.
To serve, fluff the rice gently to mix the jewels of orange and nuts. Platter the rice and crown it with the golden chicken fillets. Garnish with extra pistachios for a royal finish.

english_name: Royal Golden Jewel Rice with Garden Vegetables
description: A KALEIDOSCOPE OF VIBRANT GARDEN VEGETABLES AND TENDER SEARED CHICKEN CRADLED IN AROMATIC SAFFRON-KISSED RICE.

instructions.text: In a glass bowl, massage the cubed chicken with the juice of the grated onion, sea salt, and cracked black pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to ensure the enzymes tenderize the poultry.
Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Sizzle the marinated chicken until it develops a gorgeous golden-brown crust and is cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, parboil the basmati rice. Drain the rice when the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm, 'al dente' core, usually after 7 minutes.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, begin the royal assembly: create layers of parboiled rice followed by the golden chicken, mushrooms, bell peppers, peas, and corn. Repeat until all ingredients are used.
Drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer for that signature aroma and sprinkle the toasted sesame seeds for a sophisticated crunch.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel to trap the steam. Set on the lowest heat possible and allow the flavors to marry and the rice to become fluffy for 45 minutes.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald Green Bean Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT TAPESTRY OF FRAGRANT HERBS AND TENDER GREEN BEANS KISSED BY ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear, then parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the middle. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a wide skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat. Sauté the green beans with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes until vibrant. Stir in the chopped herb medley and fried onions, tossing for another 3 minutes until the aroma of the herbs fills your kitchen.

Prepare the pot for steaming by adding 1 tablespoon of oil to the bottom. Layer the parboiled rice and the herb-bean mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape.
Cover the pot lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap steam. Cook on low-medium heat for 10 minutes to set the crust (Tahdig), then reduce to low and steam gently for 35-40 minutes.

Create the 'Golden Touch' reduction: In a small pan, sizzle the tomato paste in 2 tablespoons of oil for 2 minutes to remove the raw taste. Whisk in the saffron infusion, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes until a rich, crimson glaze forms.
Gently fluff the rice with a fork, drizzling the saffron-tomato reduction over the top layers. Transfer to a platter, ensuring the crispy golden Tahdig from the bottom is served on the side.

english_name: Royal Persian Lamb Head and Trotter Pilaf (Kalleh Pacheh Polo)
description: A REGAL DELICACY FEATURING MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH LAMB NESTLED IN A FRAGRANT HEART OF APRICOTS AND PLUMS.

instructions.text: Place the cleaned lamb head and trotters in a large pot with an onion, turmeric, and water. Simmer gently over low heat for 5-6 hours until the meat is exceptionally tender and literally falling off the bone. Reserve one cup of the rich, gelatinous broth.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt the butter until it sizzles. Add the dried plums and apricots, sautéing for 3-4 minutes until they become glossy and slightly plump. Remove the fruit and set aside.

In the same pan with the remaining butter, sauté the crushed garlic until fragrant and golden. Stir in the dried pennyroyal, ground hogweed, and liquid kashk. Gradually pour in the reserved lamb broth, stirring constantly to create a silky, aromatic umami sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.
To assemble, layer half of the parboiled rice into a pot. Drizzle a few spoonfuls of the garlic-kashk sauce over the rice. Place the sautéed fruits in the center to create a sweet-tart heart.

Add the remaining rice, followed by the rest of the sauce. Carefully place the cooked lamb head meat and trotters on top of the rice mound. Cover with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a damkoni (kitchen towel).

Steam over low heat for 45-60 minutes. This slow process allows the rice to absorb the lamb's essence and the fruits to steam perfectly. For the 'Golden Touch,' drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top 10 minutes before serving.

english_name: Persian Royal Silk Rice (Shir Polo)
description: EXPERIENCE THE LUXURY OF TABRIZ WITH VELVETY MILK-INFUSED RICE AND GOLDEN SAFFRON MEATBALLS.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, melt the butter with the vegetable oil over medium heat. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot, stirring gently for 3 to 5 minutes to coat every grain in fat until they become slightly translucent and fragrant.

Pour in the water, milk, and salt. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then stir in half of your 'Golden Touch' saffron liquid. Allow it to cook uncovered on medium-high for about 10-12 minutes until the liquid is mostly absorbed and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface of the rice.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting, wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), and seal the pot tightly. Steam for 25 to 30 minutes to achieve a fluffy, tender texture.

While the rice steams, combine the ground meat with the grated onion and a pinch of salt. Roll into marble-sized meatballs (Kofteh Ghelgheli). Sizzle them in a hot pan with a drop of oil for 8 minutes until golden-brown and caramelized on all sides.
In the same pan, briefly sauté the raisins for 1 minute until they plump up. Do not overcook or they will become bitter.

Fluff the rice with a fork, layering it onto a platter. Crown the dish with the golden meatballs, plump raisins, and slivered pistachios. Drizzle the remaining saffron over the top for a royal finish.

english_name: Royal Persian Sardi Rice
description: A JEWELED MASTERPIECE OF AROMATIC SPICES, TENDER CARROTS, AND GOLDEN RICE.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed skillet, sizzle the ground meat over medium-high heat with a touch of oil. Break it apart with a wooden spoon until browned and crumbly, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the fried onions, salt, pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, cumin, caraway, and coriander seeds. Let the spices toast with the meat for 3 minutes until the aroma fills your kitchen.
In a separate small pot, simmer the julienned carrots with half a cup of water over medium heat. Cook for 10 minutes until the water is fully absorbed and the carrots are tender-crisp.
Add a knob of butter to the carrots, toss in the raisins, and sauté for 2 minutes until the raisins plump up and shine. Fold this mixture into the spiced meat.

In a large non-stick pot, layer the parboiled rice with the meat and carrot mixture. If using the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer. Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to develop a golden Tahdig crust.

english_name: Persian Sun-Kissed Tomato Rice (Dami Gojeh Farangi)
description: A VIBRANT RUBY MASTERPIECE: FLUFFY TOMATO-INFUSED GRAINS WITH A CRISPY GOLDEN HEART.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted warm water for 15 minutes to ensure long, elegant grains.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Sizzle the tomato paste for 2 minutes until it darkens into a deep rust color and releases its aromatic oils.
Stir in the tomato juice and beef stock. Bring the vibrant red liquid to a gentle boil, allowing the flavors to marry.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot along with the diced potatoes and salt. If you desire the Royal Upgrade, drizzle your bloomed saffron over the surface now.
Cook uncovered over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally but gently, until the liquid has been mostly absorbed by the rice and small steam holes appear on the surface.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Reduce heat to the lowest setting and let the rice steam for 30 minutes until fluffy and a golden crust forms at the bottom.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Aromatic Chicken Rice
description: A VIBRANT SYMPHONY OF BUTTER-SEARED CHICKEN AND ZESTY LIME-INFUSED BASMATI.

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Sauté the diced onions for 6 minutes until they become translucent and start to develop a beautiful golden shimmer.
Add the chicken cubes to the pan. Sizzle for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender, fully cooked, and carries a light golden-brown sear on all sides.
Incorporate the tomatoes, scallions, chili, and bell peppers. Sauté for 3 minutes, allowing the vegetables to soften and create a vibrant, aromatic base that coats the chicken.
Season with salt and cracked pepper. If you desire the Golden Touch, fold in your bloomed saffron now to elevate the dish to royal status.
Gently fold the cooked rice into the mixture. Toss for 3 minutes over medium-low heat to ensure every grain is warm and infused with the savory pan juices.
Plate the rice immediately, garnishing with fresh basil and a generous squeeze of lime to awaken the flavors.

english_name: Royal Semnani Slow-Braised Lamb Neck
description: EXPERIENCE THE VELVETY ELEGANCE OF PERSIA'S FINEST SLOW-COOKED LAMB NECK.

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium heat. Sauté the diced onions for approximately 12-15 minutes, stirring frequently until they reach a deep, glistening golden-brown caramelization.
Increase the heat slightly and add the lamb neck. Sear the meat on all sides for about 8 minutes until a beautiful brown crust forms, locking in the succulent juices.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry for 2-3 minutes. This step is crucial to cook out the raw metallic taste and develop a rich, savory base.
Pour in the golden bloomed saffron and add enough boiling water to reach halfway up the side of the meat. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to the lowest setting.
Cover tightly and simmer very slowly for 2.5 to 3 hours. The meat should be 'fork-tender' and nearly falling off the bone.
Ten minutes before serving, sprinkle in the ground cinnamon. This late addition ensures the warm, woody aroma stays vibrant without becoming bitter. Allow the sauce to thicken into a rich glaze.

english_name: Royal Saffron & Yogurt Rice Jewel (Tahchin Shirazi)
description: A SHATTERING GOLDEN CRUST MEETS A FRAGRANT SAFFRON HEART IN THIS ULTIMATE PERSIAN RICE CAKE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water for 7-9 minutes. The rice should be 'al dente'—soft on the edges but still firm in the very center. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking.
Prepare the 'Golden Touch' by grinding your saffron with a pinch of sugar and melting it over two ice cubes. This extraction method ensures the most vibrant crimson hue and a deep, royal aroma.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the yogurt, three whole eggs, one extra yolk, and the bloomed saffron until a smooth, sunshine-yellow custard forms. Fold in half of the parboiled rice gently to ensure every grain is coated in the velvet mixture.
Generously coat the bottom and sides of a heavy-bottomed glass baking dish or non-stick pot with oil. This is crucial for creating the legendary 'Tahdig' crust.
Spread the yogurt-rice mixture into the bottom of the dish, pressing down firmly with a spatula to create an even, compact base layer.
Layer the shredded chicken evenly over the rice, followed by the remaining white parboiled rice. Drizzle a small amount of oil and the remaining saffron water over the top.

Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil. Place in a preheated oven at 200°C (390°F) for 30 minutes to set the crust, then reduce the heat to 160°C (320°F) for another 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the rice to steam into fluffy perfection.
The Grand Reveal: Carefully invert the dish onto a flat platter. The result should be a solid, golden-brown cake. Garnish with sautéed barberries and pistachio slivers for a jewel-toned finish.

english_name: Royal Persian Spinach Tahchin with Golden Saffron Crust
description: A SYMPHONY OF CRUNCHY GOLD AND EMERALD SPINACH, CROWNED WITH GLISTENING JEWELED FRUITS.

instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, yogurt, half of the bloomed saffron, and a pinch of salt until velvety. Gently fold in half of your parboiled rice until every grain is dressed in gold.

Generously coat a non-stick Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed glass baking dish with oil. Spread the saffron-rice mixture into the bottom, pressing firmly with a spatula to create a solid foundation for the crust.
Briefly sauté the barberries in a small pan with a teaspoon of oil and the sugar until they puff up like glowing rubies. Sprinkle half of these and a handful of pistachios over the rice layer.
Distribute your shredded meat evenly over the barberries, pressing down lightly to embed it into the rice layer below.

Mix the remaining rice with the chopped spinach, the rest of the yogurt-egg mixture, and the remaining saffron. Layer this emerald mixture over the meat, smoothing the top into a perfectly flat surface.
Cover tightly with foil and bake in a preheated oven at 360°F (180°C) for 2 hours. This slow-bake is the secret to a thick, uniform Tahdig crust that shatters beautifully.
Allow the dish to rest for 5 minutes, then carefully invert it onto a grand serving platter. Garnish with the remaining jeweled barberries and pistachios before slicing into elegant wedges.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin with Golden Eggplant & Shredded Chicken
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CROWN OF SAFFRON RICE FEATURING A CRISPY TAHDIG SHELL AND A TENDER HEART OF EGGPLANT AND CHICKEN.

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, vigorously whisk the eggs until smooth, then fold in the thick yogurt and the aromatic saffron water until you achieve a vibrant, sunshine-yellow custard.
Season the yogurt mixture with salt and pepper, then gently fold in your parboiled rice until every grain is luxuriously coated in the golden binder.
Generously grease a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot or glass baking dish with oil. Spread a dense layer of the saffron rice at the bottom, pressing down firmly to create the foundation for the crust.
Arrange a layer of the fried eggplant rounds followed by the shredded chicken over the rice, ensuring you leave a small margin at the edges to prevent sticking.
Cover the fillings with the remaining saffron rice, smoothing the surface with the back of a spoon to seal the layers.

Cover the dish tightly with foil, piercing a few small holes with a fork to allow steam to escape. Bake in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F) for 90 minutes until the bottom is deeply caramelized and crispy.
Carefully flip the Tahchin onto a serving platter to reveal the golden 'Tahdig' crust. Garnish with the glistening sautéed barberries and serve immediately while the exterior is perfectly crunchy.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin with Golden Walnuts and Ruby Barberries
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN RICE CAKE FEATURING A CRUNCHY SAFFRON CRUST AND A RICH HEART OF LAMB, WALNUTS, AND TART BARBERRIES.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet and sauté the ground lamb with the caramelized onions over medium-high heat. Break the meat apart with a spoon until beautifully browned and sizzling.

Season the meat with turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Fold in the crushed walnuts and ruby-red barberries. Pour in half of your bloomed saffron, cover, and let the flavors marry over low heat for 10 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the strained yogurt, 4 whole eggs, 1 egg yolk, the remaining bloomed saffron, and a tablespoon of oil until you achieve a silky, golden-orange custard.
Gently fold the parboiled rice into the yogurt-egg custard. Ensure every grain of rice is luxuriously coated in the aromatic saffron mixture, turning the rice a vibrant sun-kissed yellow.

Generously grease a non-stick baking dish. Press half of the saffron rice into the bottom. Spread the savory lamb and walnut mixture evenly over the top, leaving a small margin at the edges, then seal the masterpiece with the remaining rice.
Tightly cover the dish with aluminum foil and prick a few steam vents. Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 75 to 90 minutes until the edges are deep golden and the bottom forms a legendary, crunchy crust.

english_name: Persian Royal Sour Cherry Jewel Cake (Albaloo Tahchin)
description: A BREATHTAKING RUBY-RED RICE CAKE THAT BALANCES TART CHERRY ELEGANCE WITH BUTTERY PERFECTION.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-10 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking.
In a small saucepan, combine the pitted sour cherries and sugar. Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, allowing the cherries to release their vibrant juices and form a light syrup.
Increase the heat slightly and whisk in the butter. Let the mixture bubble gently for 5 minutes until the syrup thickens into a glossy, ruby-red glaze. Remove from heat.
Line a heatproof glass or ceramic baking dish with heat-resistant food wrap (plastic wrap), ensuring enough overhang to cover the top. Lightly grease the wrap with oil to ensure a flawless release.

In a large bowl, gently fold the parboiled rice with the cherries and half of the syrup. For the 'Golden Touch,' fold the bloomed saffron into a handful of the rice before mixing everything together. The rice should be beautifully stained but not soaking wet.

Transfer the rice mixture into the prepared dish. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon to compact the grains—this is the secret to a sliceable cake texture. Fold the excess wrap over the top to seal in the moisture.
Place the dish in the center of a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F). Bake for 35-40 minutes until the rice is set and the aromas of sweet cherry and butter fill your kitchen.

Remove from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes. Carefully peel back the wrap, place a serving platter over the dish, and flip it with confidence. Remove the plastic to reveal your ruby-crusted masterpiece.

english_name: Royal Aromatic Chicken & Mushroom Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT KALEIDOSCOPE OF AROMATIC SPICES AND TENDER POULTRY DANCING IN GOLDEN SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for about 7-9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking process.

Heat oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken fillets, seasoning with salt and pepper. Sear the chicken until the exterior turns an opaque ivory color and the juices begin to seal in.
Incorporate the minced garlic, grated ginger, and curry powder. Stir-fry for 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a warm, spicy fragrance.
Add the sliced mushrooms and the pre-fried golden onions. Continue to sauté for 4-5 minutes until the mushrooms have softened and developed a slight golden hue.
Toss in the vibrant bell peppers and drizzle in the liquid saffron. Sauté for another 3 minutes, allowing the saffron to paint the ingredients in a royal yellow glow.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, create layers: start with a base of parboiled rice, then spread a generous portion of the chicken and mushroom mixture. Repeat the layers, finishing with a crown of white rice.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (dam-kani) to trap the steam. Cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and a crispy crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.
Gently fluff the rice and mound it onto a platter. Garnish with the remaining chicken and pepper mixture for a visual masterpiece.

english_name: Golden Silk Road Noodle Rice with Tender Lamb
description: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN COMFORT FEAST DESIGNED TO UNTIE THE KNOTS OF LIFE.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot, place the lamb chunks with one sliced onion and a bay leaf. Cover with 7 cups of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 120 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and the broth is rich.
While the lamb braises, bloom the 'Golden Touch': steep the ground saffron in 1/2 cup of boiling water, covering it with a small plate to trap the aroma.

In a large pot of salted boiling water, add the pre-soaked rice. Exactly 5 minutes before the rice is ready to be drained (al dente), add the toasted noodles to the same pot. Boil together for the remaining 5 minutes.
Drain the rice and noodle mixture into a fine-mesh colander. Rinse briefly with lukewarm water to remove excess starch and prevent sticking.

Prepare the Tahdig: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in the pot. Layer the bottom with flatbread or potato slices. Mound the rice and noodle mixture on top, forming a pyramid shape. Poke five holes into the rice with a spoon handle to allow steam to circulate.

Mix 2 tablespoons of oil with 1/2 cup of hot water and drizzle over the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and seal the pot tightly. Steam on low heat for 60 minutes until a golden crust forms at the bottom.

In a skillet, caramelize the second onion in oil until deeply golden. Stir in turmeric and the cooked lamb chunks. Sauté for 5 minutes, adding a splash of the bloomed saffron and a ladle of the lamb broth for a glossy finish.
To serve, plate the aromatic rice, layering the succulent lamb in the center. Drizzle with the remaining saffron water and the concentrated lamb reduction. Serve with the crispy Tahdig on the side.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald & Ruby Persian Pilaf (Nokhod Polo)
description: A VIBRANT GARDEN-TO-TABLE MASTERPIECE FEATURING FLUFFY SAFFRON RICE, SWEET PEAS, AND CRISPY GOLDEN POTATOES.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.
In a small pot, simmer the peas in salted water for 5 minutes until parboiled. Drain and immediately shock in ice water to preserve that vibrant emerald green color.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry the potato cubes until they develop a crisp, golden-brown exterior. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the onions with turmeric until they are caramelized and translucent, releasing a sweet, earthy aroma.
Pour the tomato puree into the onions. Increase the heat and stir constantly until the moisture evaporates, leaving a rich, concentrated ruby-red sauce.
Add 4 cups of water, a pinch of salt, and a splash of oil to the tomato base. Bring to a vigorous boil.
Gently fold in the parboiled peas and the soaked, drained rice into the boiling pot.
Once the liquid has reduced by half, gently stir in the golden potato cubes, ensuring they are distributed evenly throughout the rice.
When the water is fully absorbed, drizzle the 'Golden Touch' of bloomed saffron over the top. Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid (Damkoni) to trap the steam perfectly.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting and allow the pilaf to 'Dam' (steam) for 60 minutes until a crispy Tahdig forms at the bottom and the grains are tender.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Seasonal Jewel Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT KALEIDOSCOPE OF SEASONAL VEGETABLES NESTLED IN FLUFFY, SAFFRON-KISSED BASMATI RICE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.

In a large skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat. Sauté the cubed potatoes until they develop a light golden crust. Add the green beans, peas, and corn, stir-frying for 5-7 minutes until the vegetables are vibrant and slightly tender.
Incorporate the chopped tomato, turmeric, garlic powder, and black pepper. Stir frequently for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down into a fragrant, concentrated sauce that coats the vegetables.

Pour in 2 cups of boiling water, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the vegetables are perfectly tender. Allow this mixture to cool slightly before layering.

Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 7-10 minutes. The grains should be 'al dente'—soft on the outside but still firm to the bite in the center. Drain and rinse gently with cool water.

Prepare the pot with oil and a thin layer of sliced potatoes or flatbread for the Tahdig. Layer the rice and the vegetable mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Sprinkle a touch of cinnamon between each layer.

For the 'Royal Upgrade', drizzle your bloomed Saffron over the top layer of rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes until steam rises, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 60-90 minutes for a perfect crust and aromatic finish.
Gently fold the layers together with a spatula to distribute the colors and flavors, then serve on a large platter topped with the crunchy Tahdig pieces.

english_name: Royal Saffron Lamb Shank with Dill & Fava Bean Rice
description: A MAJESTIC SYMPHONY OF MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH LAMB AND AROMATIC EMERALD RICE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak in lukewarm water with 2 tablespoons of salt for at least 2 hours or overnight to ensure long, fluffy grains.

Place the lamb shank in a heavy-bottomed pot with one sliced onion and a bay leaf. Cover with water and bring to a vigorous boil, skimming off any foam. Reduce heat and simmer gently for 120 minutes until the meat is tender and starting to pull away from the bone.

In a large pot of boiling salted water, blanch the fava beans for 15 minutes. Add the soaked rice to the same pot and boil for another 5-7 minutes until the rice grains are soft on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente).

Drain the rice and fava bean mixture. In a clean non-stick pot, add 2 tablespoons of oil. Create a base layer of rice, then alternate layers of the rice-bean mix with the chopped fresh dill. Drizzle half of your bloomed saffron over the top. Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to develop a crispy golden Tahdig.

While the rice steams, prepare the meat glaze. Sauté the remaining onion in oil until golden brown, stir in turmeric and tomato paste for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the cooked lamb shank, the remaining saffron, and 1 cup of the strained lamb broth. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens into a rich, aromatic lacquer.

To serve, mound the fragrant rice on a large platter, ensuring the bright green dill and yellow saffron grains are well mixed. Place the succulent lamb shank in the center and pour the reduced silken sauce over the meat.

english_name: Golden Saffron & Parmesan Risotto-Style Rice
description: A LUXURIOUS FUSION WHERE SILK ROAD AROMATICS MEET THE BOLD CREAMINESS OF AGED PARMESAN.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for about 5 minutes until translucent and soft, ensuring they do not brown to keep the color pure.
Add the rinsed rice to the pot. Stir well for 1-2 minutes to coat every grain in the aromatic butter, lightly toasting the rice to release a nutty fragrance.

Pour in the broth and add the 'Royal Golden Touch'—the saffron. Stir once to distribute the crimson threads, which will soon bleed into a majestic sun-yellow hue. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover with a tight-fitting lid. Reduce heat to low and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender and velvety.
Remove from heat. Gently fold in the grated Parmesan cheese, allowing it to melt into the grains, creating a luxurious, creamy finish. Serve immediately while the aroma is at its peak.

english_name: Silk Road Royal Surf & Turf Fried Rice with Curried Kofta
description: A MAJESTIC FUSION OF SUCCULENT MEATS, FRAGRANT SPICES, AND SEA-FRESH SHRIMP DANCING ON A BED OF AROMATIC RICE.

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground meat, grated onion, chili powder, curry powder, and egg white. Knead vigorously for 5 minutes until the proteins bind and the mixture is tacky, then roll into petite, uniform meatballs.

Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the meatballs for 5-7 minutes until they develop a deep golden-brown crust and are cooked through. Drain on a paper towel and thread onto small decorative skewers.

Whisk the 2 eggs with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. In a hot non-stick pan with a touch of peanut oil, pour the egg mixture to create a thin omelette. Once set, remove, slice half into ribbons and half into small squares.
In a large wok or heavy-bottomed skillet, heat the remaining peanut oil until shimmering. Sauté the sliced onions, garlic, and julienned bell peppers until the onions are translucent and fragrant.

Increase the heat to high. Add the chicken breast cubes and lamb/beef ribbons. Season with the ground pepper and sear for 8-10 minutes, tossing constantly until the meats are succulent and caramelized.

Add the shrimp and bean sprouts. Sauté for 2 minutes until the shrimp turn pink. Fold in the chilled rice, breaking up any clumps, and toss for 3 minutes until the rice is heated through and starts to sizzle.
For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle your bloomed saffron over a portion of the rice. Fold in the cilantro and the square-cut omelette pieces for a final minute.
Plate the aromatic rice in a grand mound. Garnish with the omelette ribbons and crown with the curried kofta skewers. Serve immediately.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Aromatic Silk Road Burritos
description: A GOLDEN GLOBAL FUSION: FRAGRANT SPICED RICE MEETS MELTY CHEDDAR IN A TOASTY TORTILLA HUG.

instructions.text: Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for exactly 7 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm to the bite; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Sauté the diced onion for 8-10 minutes until it becomes translucent and takes on a delicate golden shimmer.
Add the ground cloves and oregano to the center of the pan, blooming them in the hot oil for 30 seconds to release their deep, earthy essential oils.
Fold in the parboiled rice and grated tomato pulp. Cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, allowing the rice to absorb the tomato essence and finish cooking until fluffy.
In a separate pot, poach the chicken breasts in salted water (add your Saffron here for a 'Golden Touch') for 15-20 minutes until tender. Let cool, then shred with two forks into succulent ribbons.
Gently fold the shredded chicken and the grated cheddar cheese into the aromatic rice mixture until the cheese just begins to melt, binding the ingredients into a rich filling.
Preheat your oven to 160°C (320°F) to ensure a warm environment for your final masterpieces.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and place them over a pot of steaming water for 3 minutes until they are soft, warm, and ready to be shaped.
Spoon a generous portion of filling into each tortilla, roll them tightly into neat parcels, and place in a baking dish covered with foil. Warm in the oven for 5 minutes before serving.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Aromatic Silk Road Tomato & Pea Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT FUSION WHERE BOLD MEXICAN ZEST MEETS THE REGAL ELEGANCE OF PERSIAN STEAMING TECHNIQUES.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.

Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat; add the onions and sauté for 8-10 minutes until they achieve a deep golden-brown translucency. Add the garlic in the last 2 minutes to release its fragrance without burning.

Pour the fresh tomato puree into the pot with the aromatics. Simmer for 12 minutes on medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate, intensifying the natural sugars of the tomato.
In a separate small pot, blanch the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender-crisp, then immediately shock them in ice water to preserve their vibrant emerald green color.

Drain the soaked rice and add it to the tomato base. Add the 3 cups of boiling water, crumbled bouillon, dried chilies, and the blanched peas. Gently fold the ingredients to combine without breaking the rice grains.

If using the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the surface now. Bring the liquid to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-Kesh) to trap every drop of steam.
Steam for 30 minutes. Once finished, turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork to reveal a masterpiece of aromatic, separated grains.

original_name: پلوی ساده با طعم هل و میخک
english_name: Royal Aromatic Rice with Cardamom and Cloves
description: A SYMPHONY OF FRAGRANCE CAPTURED IN EVERY GOLDEN GRAIN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak with sea salt in plenty of water for at least 2 hours to achieve maximum grain length.
In a small saucepan, bring the chicken broth to a gentle simmer. Add the cracked cardamom pods and whole cloves, allowing them to steep for 5 minutes until their warm, floral oils are fully released.

Drain the soaked rice and place it into a heavy-bottomed pot. Add the 2 cups of water, the spice-infused broth, the oil, and the 'Golden Touch'—the bloomed saffron. Stir once gently to distribute the color.

Bring the pot to a boil over medium-high heat. Once the water has mostly evaporated and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface of the rice, wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (the Damkani technique) and seal the pot tightly.
Reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting and let the rice steam undisturbed for 45 to 60 minutes, creating a fragrant, fluffy masterpiece with perfectly separated grains.

english_name: Springtime Wild Herb & Braised Lamb Pilaf (Sheng Polo)
description: A RARE MOUNTAIN TREASURE OF WILD HERBS AND TENDER LAMB BENEATH A GOLDEN SAFFRON VEIL.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 to 3 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.
Thoroughly wash the Sheng herbs to remove any mountain soil. Pat dry and chop into 1-inch segments. Ensure they are bone-dry before the next step to prevent steaming.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat. Sauté the julienned onions until they turn a deep, translucent gold, roughly 8-10 minutes.

Add the lamb cubes to the golden onions. Sear the meat for 5-7 minutes until a beautiful mahogany crust forms. Stir in the turmeric and half of your bloomed saffron to infuse the meat with a royal aroma.
Pour in 1.5 cups of boiling water, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 60-75 minutes until the lamb is melt-in-your-mouth tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick, savory essence.

Bring a large pot of water with 2 tablespoons of salt to a rolling boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. In the final 2 minutes of boiling, toss in the chopped Sheng herbs to blanch them with the rice.
Test the rice: it should be soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (al dente). Drain the rice and herbs through a fine-mesh sieve and rinse quickly with cool water.

To build the masterpiece: Coat the bottom of a non-stick pot with oil. Layer your potato slices or bread for the Tahdig. Mound the rice-herb mixture into a pyramid shape, poking holes with a spoon handle to allow steam to escape.
Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-low for 45 minutes until a 'cloud' of aromatic steam rises and the crust is perfectly crisp.
Drizzle the remaining bloomed saffron and a touch of melted butter over the rice. Serve the fluffy herb rice topped with the succulent braised lamb.

english_name: Royal Persian Aromatic Fava Bean & Dill Rice
description: A FRAGRANT EMERALD MASTERPIECE FEATURING BUTTERY BASMATI AND VELVETY FAVA BEANS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear. Parboil in salted boiling water for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the center—then drain in a fine-mesh sieve.
In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, melt one-third of the butter. Spread a thin, even layer of the parboiled rice across the bottom to create the foundation for a golden 'Tadig' crust.

Begin layering the masterpiece: sprinkle a quarter of the vibrant fava beans and a generous handful of minced dill over the rice. Repeat the layers, tapering the rice into a pyramid shape to allow optimal steam circulation, ending with a layer of white rice.
Pour half a cup of water around the edges of the pot. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes to jumpstart the steaming process and set the crust.

Melt the remaining butter and drizzle it luxuriously over the rice. Evenly dust the cinnamon, cumin seeds, and chili powder over the top. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) and seal the pot tightly to trap every aromatic molecule.
Reduce the heat to the lowest setting and allow the rice to steam gently for 25 to 30 minutes until perfectly fluffy and fragrant.

The Royal Touch: Bloom the ground saffron in two tablespoons of hot water. Mix a small portion of the cooked rice with the saffron liquid until it turns a deep sun-kissed gold. Garnish the main dish with this golden rice and fresh dill sprigs before serving.

english_name: Aromatic Black-Eyed Pea Jewel Rice with Golden Soy Koofteh
description: A SYMPHONY OF EARTHY LEGUMES AND FRAGRANT SPICES TOPPED WITH CRISPY UMAMI-RICH VEGETARIAN KOOFTEH.

instructions.text: Hydrate the soy protein in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain. Boil it in fresh water for 5 minutes to remove the raw bean scent. Drain again and squeeze firmly until bone-dry; this ensures the soy absorbs our aromatics rather than staying watery.
Simmer the black-eyed peas in salted water for 20-25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. They should have a slight bite—mushy beans are the enemy of a perfect Polo.

Sauté two-thirds of your onions in oil until translucent and starting to turn golden. Stir in the turmeric and cinnamon, letting the spices bloom for 30 seconds. Fold in the cooked black-eyed peas and season with salt.
Parboil your rice in a large pot of boiling salted water until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside with a firm core (usually 7-8 minutes). Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, layer the rice and the pea-onion mixture, forming a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes in the rice to let steam escape. Cover with a kitchen towel and lid, steaming on low heat for 40 minutes.

Prepare the 'Koofteh Rizeh': Grate the remaining onion and squeeze out excess juice. Mix with the prepared soy, black pepper, salt, and chickpea flour. Knead until tacky, roll into marble-sized balls, and fry in oil until deeply bronzed and crispy.

For the finale, melt the butter with your bloomed saffron. Gently fluff the steamed rice and drizzle this liquid gold over the top. Serve on a platter, crowning the aromatic rice with your crispy soy koofteh.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin with Velvety Spinach and Savory Beef
description: THE GOLDEN CROWN OF PERSIAN CUISINE REVEALING A HEART OF VELVETY SPINACH.

instructions.text: Bloom the saffron by mixing the powder with 3 tablespoons of boiling water; cover and let it steep over a simmering kettle for 10 minutes to extract the deep crimson essence.
Wash the Basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the grains elongate beautifully.

In a heavy-bottomed skillet, sauté one sliced onion in oil until it reaches a deep golden caramelization. Add the chopped spinach and a pinch of salt, sautéing until the moisture has fully evaporated.

Grate the second onion into the ground beef. Season with salt, pepper, and one tablespoon of the bloomed saffron. Brown the meat in a separate pan until fully cooked and the juices have been reabsorbed.
Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain when the grains are soft on the outside but still firm (al dente) in the center.

In a large glass bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the yogurt and the remaining bloomed saffron until a vibrant golden custard forms. Gently fold the parboiled rice into this mixture until every grain is coated.

Generously oil a deep non-stick pot. Press half of the saffron rice into the bottom. Layer the spinach mixture followed by the beef, leaving a small border at the edges. Top with the remaining rice and press down firmly.
Place the lid on with a clean kitchen towel wrap (Damkoni). Cook on medium-low heat for 90 to 120 minutes until a thick, glass-like golden crust (Tahdig) forms on the bottom and sides.

english_name: Royal Persian Chicken Tahchin (The Saffron Rice Cake)
description: THE GOLDEN JEWEL OF PERSIAN CUISINE: A SHATTERING CRISPY CRUST REVEALING VELVET SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Place the chicken in a pot with onions, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Add 2 cups of water and simmer gently for 45 minutes until tender. Reserve 1/2 cup of the concentrated chicken broth and shred the meat into large, succulent chunks.

Bloom your ground saffron by placing it over a small ice cube; the slow melt extracts a more vibrant crimson hue. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the yogurt, bloomed saffron, half of the oil, and the reserved chicken broth.
Submerge the shredded chicken into the saffron-yogurt mixture. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. This marination is the secret to the velvet-soft texture of the meat.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, parboil the rice for 7-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still firm (al dente) in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.
Mix 3 spatulas of the parboiled rice into the remaining yogurt marinade to create the base. Pour the remaining oil into a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot (or glass Pyrex dish).

Spread the yogurt-rice mixture firmly across the bottom of the pot to create the 'Tahdig' layer. Add a layer of marinated chicken, followed by a layer of plain rice. Repeat until all ingredients are used, pressing down firmly between layers.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani). Cook on medium-low heat for 90 minutes. This slow-steam creates the iconic golden-brown crust.
Carefully invert the pot onto a large serving platter. The Tahchin should emerge as a solid, glistening golden cake. Garnish with sautéed barberries and pistachios.

english_name: Persian Golden Lentil & Carrot Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT ONE-POT MASTERPIECE OF EARTHY LENTILS AND SUN-KISSED CARROTS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt one tablespoon of ghee over medium heat. Add the turmeric and sizzle for 30 seconds until the aroma fills your kitchen.
Incorporate the fried onions, lentils, and 1.5 cups of water. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the lentils are al dente (half-cooked).
Add the julienned carrots to the pot. Continue to simmer for another 5-7 minutes until the carrots begin to soften and release their natural sweetness.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes to deepen the color. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot, stirring gently to coat the grains in the golden oil.
Add enough boiling water to cover the rice by about half an inch. Sprinkle with rice spice and the remaining ghee. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle it over the top now.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani). Steam on low heat for 35-40 minutes until a golden crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.

english_name: Aromatic Black Pepper Rice with Golden Saffron Chicken
description: A BOLD SYMPHONY OF FIERY BLACK PEPPER AND REGAL SAFFRON INFUSED INTO EVERY GRAIN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a large pot, place the chicken pieces and cover with 4 cups of water. Bring to a vigorous boil and carefully skim off any grey foam that rises to the surface for a clean, pure broth.

Add the chopped onions, turmeric, and carrots to the pot. Infuse the broth with half of your bloomed saffron 'Royal Upgrade' and a generous pinch of salt. Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and aromatic.
Remove the chicken and carrots. Strain the golden chicken broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, discarding the solids. Measure the broth; you will need exactly 4-5 cups for the rice.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add the drained rice and the measured chicken broth. Stir in the whole black peppercorns. Bring to a boil over high heat until the liquid evaporates and small 'steam holes' form on the surface of the rice.

Drizzle melted butter and the remaining saffron over the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), seal tightly, and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to develop a crisp golden crust (Tahdig).
Serve the fluffy pepper-flecked rice on a platter, crowning it with the succulent saffron chicken pieces.

english_name: Aromatic Tarragon Pan-Kabab
description: A SYMPHONY OF FRESH HERBS AND SIZZLING MEAT THAT REFINES THE ART OF THE PERSIAN PAN-KABAB.

instructions.text: Prepare the aromatic heart of the dish by washing the tarragon and drying it thoroughly. Finely mince the leaves to release their signature anise-scented oils.

Grate the onion using a fine grater. Crucially, squeeze the grated onion through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove all excess liquid; this ensures your kababs remain firm and don't become soggy.
In a large chilled mixing bowl, combine the ground meat, prepared onion, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Use your hands to integrate the spices deeply into the proteins.

Whisk the eggs and yogurt together, then add them to the meat along with the chopped tarragon. Knead the mixture vigorously for at least 5 minutes until it becomes tacky and uniform—this develops the structure.

Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Shape the mixture into small, elegant patties or spread it entirely across the pan, scoring it into strips. Fry until a deep, mahogany-golden crust forms on one side (about 5-6 minutes), then flip and repeat.
Serve immediately over a bed of fluffy basmati rice. For the Golden Touch, drizzle your bloomed saffron over the center of the rice for a royal presentation.

english_name: Royal Persian Lentil Rice with Golden Chicken
description: EARTHY LENTILS AND FLUFFY BASMATI CROWNED WITH SUCCULENT GOLDEN CHICKEN AND SAFFRON AMBER.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 1 hour to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.
Place lentils in a pot with water and a pinch of salt. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. Drain and set aside.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with plenty of salt. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 7-8 minutes. Two minutes before draining, stir in the cooked lentils. Drain the rice-lentil mixture once the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm bite in the center.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add a splash of oil. Mound the rice and lentil mixture into a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes with the handle of a spoon to let steam escape. Cover with a kitchen towel and lid, then steam on low heat for 35-40 minutes to achieve a perfect crust (Tahdig).

While the rice steams, heat oil in a large skillet. Sauté the onions until they turn a deep, translucent gold. Add the chicken cubes and season with salt and pepper. Sear until the chicken is succulent and browned.
Toss the diced bell pepper into the skillet. Stir-fry for 5 minutes until the pepper is softened and its aroma melds with the chicken and onions.
In a small pan, lightly toast the almonds in a teaspoon of butter until fragrant. For the Royal Upgrade, stir your bloomed saffron into the almonds and a small portion of the cooked rice.
Plate the fluffy lentil rice, top with the savory chicken mixture, and garnish generously with the golden saffron-infused almonds.

english_name: Persian Spinach Rice with Velvet Meatballs (Esfenaj Polo)
description: VIBRANT PERSIAN SPINACH RICE CROWNED WITH GOLDEN VELVET MEATBALLS AND CRUNCHY BREAD TAHDIG.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for 30 minutes to ensure maximum grain length.

Place the cleaned spinach in a large pot over medium heat without adding water. Let it wilt in its own steam for 5-7 minutes until the moisture has completely evaporated, intensifying its earthy flavor.

In a bowl, knead the ground meat with one grated onion (squeezed of excess juice), salt, pepper, and half the turmeric. Form into hazelnut-sized 'Kofteh Rizeh' and sear in a hot pan with oil until they develop a deep, savory golden crust.
