Increase heat slightly and add the diced beef. Sear the meat until it is browned on all sides, locking in the juices. Stir in the grated garlic, black pepper, and half of the Advieh spice.

Pour in 2 cups of boiling water and the pre-cooked peas. Cover and simmer gently on low heat for 45-60 minutes until the beef is melt-in-your-mouth tender and the liquid has mostly reduced into a thick, aromatic sauce.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the middle. Drain and rinse with cool water.
In a non-stick pot, add a splash of oil and a drizzle of the bloomed saffron. Layer the rice and the meat-vegetable mixture, building a pyramid shape. Sprinkle the remaining Advieh between layers.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes to set the crust (Tahdig), then reduce to low and steam for 45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and aromatic.

english_name: Royal Silk Road Noodle Rice with Tender Lamb
description: A TIMELESS PERSIAN MASTERPIECE OF TOASTED NOODLES AND SUCCULENT MEAT CROWNED WITH GOLDEN JEWELS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 60 minutes to ensure maximum grain length.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, sauté the onions in olive oil over medium heat until they achieve a deep golden-caramel color. Add the meat cubes and sear until browned on all sides, releasing a rich aroma.
Stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Pour in 1.5 cups of boiling water, cover tightly, and simmer gently for 75 minutes until the meat is melt-in-your-mouth tender.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice. Precisely 3 minutes before the rice reaches 'al dente' texture, stir in the toasted noodles. Boil for the final 3 minutes, then drain and rinse with lukewarm water.

Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in the pot. Mound the rice and noodle mixture back into the pot in a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes for steam to escape, cover with a cloth-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to create the perfect 'Tahdig' crust.
Briefly sauté the raisins, almonds, and optional barberries in the remaining butter for 2 minutes until the raisins plump up and the nuts become fragrant.
Platter the fluffy rice, nestle the tender meat on top, and crown with the jeweled nut mixture and a drizzle of the Royal Saffron infusion.

english_name: Silk Road Bulgur & Rice Pilaf (Dami Balghur)
description: AN ANCIENT HARMONY OF EARTHY BULGUR AND SILKY BASMATI CRUSTED IN GOLD.

instructions.text: Place the bulgur wheat in a small pot with 1 cup of water. Simmer gently over low heat for 30 minutes until the grains are tender yet retain a slight bite (al dente). Drain any excess water and set aside.

In a large non-stick pot (pot-e-dami), heat the oil and sauté the golden fried onions with turmeric and salt. Let the spices bloom in the oil for 2 minutes until the aroma fills your kitchen with a warm, earthy scent.
Pour the remaining 4.5 cups of water into the pot. Increase the heat to medium-high and bring the aromatic liquid to a rolling boil.
Gently add the soaked rice (drained) and the pre-cooked bulgur to the boiling water. Stir once to combine the grains evenly without breaking the delicate rice kernels.
Continue boiling uncovered until the water has evaporated and small steam 'craters' appear on the surface of the rice. This ensures the grains will be fluffy rather than sticky.

Optional: For the Golden Touch, drizzle your bloomed saffron over the top. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni), cover tightly, and steam on the lowest heat setting for 40 minutes to develop a perfect golden crust (Tahdig) at the bottom.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald Rice
description: A VIBRANT ONE-POT MASTERPIECE OF JEWEL-TONED GREENS AND FLUFFY AROMATIC BASMATI.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice in cold water at least three times until the water runs clear to remove excess starch for maximum fluffiness.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 6-8 minutes until golden and translucent, adding the garlic in the last 2 minutes to release its fragrance.
Fold in the chopped spinach and cilantro. Sauté for exactly 2 minutes; you want them to wilt slightly and release their oils while maintaining a vibrant, jewel-toned green.
Add the drained rice to the pot and stir gently for 1 minute, ensuring every grain is coated in the aromatic oil and herb mixture.

Pour in the broth or water, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cover with a tight-fitting lid (ideally wrapped in a clean kitchen towel) and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Turn off the heat. If using the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top. Let the pot sit undisturbed for 10 minutes to allow the steam to finish fluffing the grains.

english_name: Royal Shirazi Jeweled Rice (Jawaher Polow Style)
description: A BEJEWELED MASTERPIECE OF FRAGRANT SAFFRON, TART BERRIES, AND CRUNCHY ROYAL NUTS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water 3 to 5 times until the starch washes away and the water runs crystal clear. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with 2 tablespoons of salt. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water; parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (Al Dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

While the rice drains, melt 1 tablespoon of ghee in a pan. Sauté the barberries with sugar and rose water for 2-3 minutes over medium-low heat until they plump up and glisten like rubies. Be careful not to burn them. Set aside.

In the bottom of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, melt 2 tablespoons of ghee and add 1 tablespoon of the bloomed saffron water. Spread a thin layer of rice across the bottom to create the foundation for the golden Tahdig crust.

Mound the remaining rice into the pot in a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes in the mound with the handle of a wooden spoon to let steam escape. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) and steam on low heat for 45 minutes until a crispy crust forms at the bottom.

Once steamed, gently fluff the rice. In a small bowl, mix two spatulas of white rice with the remaining bloomed saffron until it turns a deep royal gold. Layer the white rice on a platter, then top with the saffron rice, the ruby barberries, the orange peel, and the crunch of pistachios and almonds.

english_name: Silk Road Bell Pepper Pilaf with Golden Fried Eggs
description: VIBRANT JEWELED RICE TOPPED WITH CRISPY-EDGED EGGS—A SUNSHINE FEAST IN EVERY BITE.

instructions.text: Warm the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat; add the onions and sauté for 6-8 minutes until they reach a soft, translucent gold. Stir in the garlic for the final 60 seconds until the aroma fills your kitchen.
Incorporate the vibrant bell pepper trio into the pot. Sauté for 4-5 minutes, allowing them to soften slightly while retaining their brilliant colors and snap—do not overcook them into a mush.
Gently fold the washed Basmati rice into the pepper mixture. Stir for 2 minutes to coat every grain in the aromatic oil, which ensures a fluffier texture and prevents sticking.

Pour in 4 cups of filtered water along with the turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid (wrapped in a kitchen towel for the perfect steam), and simmer for 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is fully absorbed.

While the rice rests, heat a splash of oil in a non-stick skillet. Fry the eggs until the whites are set with a crispy, lacy golden edge, but the yolks remain rich and runny. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the cooked rice now.
Fluff the rice with a fork to release the steam. Mound it onto a platter, crown with the fried eggs, and scatter the fresh green herbs over the top for a final burst of life.

english_name: Royal Golden Turmeric & Saffron Rice (Dampokhtak)
description: THE HUMBLE BAZAAR CLASSIC REIMAGINED WITH A ROYAL SAFFRON GLOW AND BUTTERY CRUNCH.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the starch clears, then soak in salted water for 30 minutes to achieve the perfect long grain.
In a small pot, simmer the yellow split peas with water and a pinch of salt for 10-12 minutes until tender but still 'al dente'. Drain and set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, sauté the grated onion in oil until translucent. Add the turmeric and sizzle for 2 minutes until the aroma is released and the oil turns a vibrant gold.
Add the drained rice and split peas into the pot. Gently fold them into the golden onion mixture, ensuring every grain is coated in turmeric oil.
Pour in enough water to cover the rice by about half an inch. Add salt and the butter. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Once the water has mostly evaporated and small steam holes appear, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel and seal tightly.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting and steam for 35 minutes to allow the flavors to marry and a golden crust (Tahdig) to form at the bottom.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald Green Pea Rice (Nokhod Farangi Polo)
description: VIBRANT EMERALD PEAS NESTLED IN FRAGRANT CLOUDS OF AROMATIC SPICED BASMATI.

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash the rice under cold water until the starch rinses away and the water runs clear. Soak in lukewarm salted water for 45 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a large non-stick pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Sauté the grated onions with turmeric until they achieve a beautiful golden-brown hue and a jammy consistency.
Add the minced garlic to the onions, stirring constantly for 2 minutes until the aroma is released without browning the garlic.
Incorporate the grated carrot, black peppercorns, and cracked cardamom pods. Sauté for 5 minutes, allowing the spices to toast and the carrots to soften into the aromatic base.
Gently fold in the green peas and sprinkle with cinnamon. Stir for 3 minutes to coat every pea in the fragrant spice oil.

Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Add boiling water until it sits roughly one inch above the rice level. Taste the water; it should be as salty as the sea. Cook uncovered on medium-high heat until the water is completely absorbed and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface.

If using the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over one corner of the rice. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap steam. Cover tightly and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Let the rice 'dem' (steam) for 45 minutes until a golden tahdig crust forms at the bottom.

english_name: Persian Royal Estamboli Rice (Estamboli Plov)
description: A SYMPHONY OF VIBRANT TOMATO-INFUSED RICE, TENDER LAMB, AND CRISPY POTATOES IN ONE ROYAL POT.

instructions.text: Place the lamb cubes in a small pot with two cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes until the meat is melt-in-your-mouth tender. Strain and reserve the precious lamb broth.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and sauté for 7 minutes until they are translucent and have reached a beautiful golden hue.

Toss in the diced bell peppers and potatoes. Sauté for another 5-8 minutes until the potatoes start to take on a slight crust. Add the cooked lamb, salt, and pepper, stirring gently to marry the flavors.

Add the tomato paste to the center of the pot. Fry the paste for 2 minutes until it turns a deep crimson and loses its raw edge—this is the secret to a vibrant color. Stir in the rice and coat every grain with the aromatic oil.

Pour in the reserved lamb broth plus 2 cups of hot water. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, stir it in now. Bring to a vigorous boil, then let it simmer uncovered until the water level drops below the rice and small steam 'craters' appear on the surface.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), cover the pot tightly, and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Allow the rice to steam for 45 minutes to develop a fluffy texture and a crisp golden bottom (Tahdig).

english_name: Persian Aromatic Polo Shooshtari
description: A ROYAL TAPESTRY OF FRAGRANT DILL, CREAMY PEAS, AND SAFFRON-KISSED CHICKEN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure maximum grain length.

In a large pot, bring water to a rolling boil with plenty of salt. Drain the soaked rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the middle (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.
In a wide skillet, sauté the chicken fillets with the pre-fried onions and ghee over medium-high heat. Sear for 6-8 minutes until the chicken develops a beautiful golden-brown crust.

Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, salt, pepper, and half of the bloomed saffron. Add a splash of water, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is succulent and the liquid has reduced to a thick glaze.
Gently fold the cooked black-eyed peas and the fresh chopped dill into the chicken mixture. Be careful not to mash the peas; you want them whole for texture.
In a non-stick pot, drizzle oil and a touch of saffron water. Layer the parboiled rice and the chicken-herb mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Top with the remaining saffron water.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and seal tightly. Cook on low heat for 45-50 minutes to allow the steam to infuse and a crispy golden crust (Tahdig) to form at the bottom.

english_name: Royal Persian Green Bean Rice (Loobia Polo with Saffron Chicken)
description: EXPERIENCE THE WARM EMBRACE OF PERSIA IN EVERY FLUFFY, CINNAMON-SCENTED GRAIN OF THIS TIMELESS MASTERPIECE.

instructions.text: Sauté the onions in a large pan with oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until they turn a deep translucent gold. Stir in the green beans and sauté for another 5 minutes until they are slightly tender and vibrant.
Add the chicken fillets to the pan. Season with turmeric, salt, and pepper. Sear the chicken until it develops a light golden-brown crust, locking in the juices.

Incorporate the tomato paste, stirring it into the oil for 2 minutes to wake up its color and sweetness. Pour in half a cup of water, cover, and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens into a rich, aromatic ragu.

While the sauce simmers, parboil your basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain the rice when the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (al dente).

In a heavy-bottomed pot, drizzle oil and a splash of bloomed saffron. Layer the rice and the chicken-bean mixture alternately, sprinkling a touch of cinnamon between each layer to create a mountain shape.

Poke three holes in the rice for steam to escape, dot with butter, and pour the remaining Royal Saffron over the top. Cover with a wrapped lid and steam on the lowest heat for 45 minutes to develop a perfect golden crust (Tahdig).

english_name: Persian Royal Raisin Rice (Kishmish Polo Ardebili)
description: A GOLDEN TREASURE FROM ARDEBIL FEATURING SUN-KISSED RAISINS AND THE ROYAL TOUCH OF SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted warm water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onions and sauté for about 10-12 minutes until they reach a deep, glistening golden-brown caramelization.
Lower the heat and stir in the raisins. Pour in the 'Golden Touch' bloomed saffron. Sauté for 2 minutes until the raisins plump up and absorb the royal aroma.
Add the slivered nuts, cinnamon, cardamom, and a pinch of salt. Stir gently for 1 minute to toast the nuts and release the essential oils of the spices.

Drain the soaked rice. In a separate pot of boiling salted water, parboil the rice for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

Gently fold the parboiled rice into the onion and raisin mixture. Sprinkle the rosewater and optional sugar over the top. Use the handle of a wooden spoon to poke a few holes in the rice to allow steam to escape.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkash), cover tightly, and steam on the lowest possible heat for 45 minutes until the rice is aromatic and perfectly fluffy.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Vegetable Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT HARVEST CELEBRATION INFUSED WITH THE GOLDEN ESSENCE OF ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure the longest possible grains.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 7-10 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

Steam the rice in a non-stick pot with a touch of oil or ghee at the bottom. Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and cook on low heat for 35 minutes until a golden crust (Tahdig) forms and the rice is fluffy.
In a separate saucepan, combine the corn, parboiled carrots, and chicken broth. Simmer over medium-low heat for 8 minutes until the liquid reduces into a savory glaze that coats the vegetables.
Whisk the bloomed saffron infusion into the vegetable mixture, stirring gently to distribute the liquid gold. Season with salt and pepper.
To serve, layer the fluffy white rice on a platter, topping each layer with the vibrant saffron-vegetable mixture for a beautiful, sunset-colored presentation.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin Rice Cake
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CRUST HIDING A CLOUD OF SAFFRON-INFUSED PERFECTION.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice repeatedly until the water runs crystal clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of boiling salted water until 'Al Dente'—firm in the center but soft on the edges (usually 7-9 minutes). Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the Greek yogurt, bloomed saffron, turmeric, and a pinch of salt until you achieve a vibrant, sunrise-gold emulsion.
Fold half of the parboiled rice into the yogurt mixture until every grain is coated in the golden velvet. This will form your signature crust.
Generously coat the bottom of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot with oil and a splash of the saffron water. Spread the yogurt-rice mixture across the bottom, pressing firmly with a spatula.
If using meat, layer it in the center, then top with the remaining white rice. Drizzle melted butter over the top and poke a few holes to let steam escape.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) and cook on low-medium heat for 45-60 minutes until the sides are visibly golden and the aroma fills the room.

english_name: Royal Saffron & Jeweled Chicken Tahchin
description: A SYMPHONY OF GOLDEN CRUNCH AND JEWELED FLAVORS: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN RICE CAKE.

instructions.text: Place the chicken breasts in a pot with the onion, turmeric, salt, and pepper; cover with water and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes until tender, then shred into large, succulent chunks.

Parboil the washed Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but retain a firm 'al dente' bite in the middle, then drain and rinse with cold water.
In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the Greek yogurt and your bloomed 'Golden Touch' saffron liquid until the mixture is a vibrant, uniform sunset orange.
Gently fold the parboiled rice into the saffron-yogurt mixture, ensuring every grain is coated in the aromatic, velvet binder.
Generously grease a heavy-bottomed glass Pyrex or non-stick pot with butter, and spread half of the saffron rice across the bottom, pressing firmly with a spatula to create a solid foundation.
Layer the shredded chicken over the rice, followed by a royal scattering of barberries, pistachios, and almonds for a burst of color and tartness.
Cover with the remaining saffron rice, smoothing the surface and poking a few holes with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape; finish by drizzling melted butter over the top.
Seal tightly with foil and bake in a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for 60 to 75 minutes, until the bottom and sides have transformed into a deep, golden-brown, shattering crust.
Allow the dish to rest for 10 minutes before carefully inverting it onto a platter or slicing into clean, architectural squares to reveal the jeweled interior.

english_name: Golden Bulgur Pilaf with Root Vegetables
description: A RUSTIC, HEARTY SYMPHONY OF WHOLE GRAINS AND CARAMELIZED ROOT VEGETABLES.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat; sauté the onions until they reach a deep, glistening golden-brown hue, roughly 8-10 minutes.
Add the ground beef, turmeric, and tomato paste to the pot. Sizzle and stir vigorously for 5 minutes until the meat is browned and the tomato paste smells fragrant and toasted.
Fold in the diced carrots and potatoes, coating them in the aromatic base. Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the vegetables soften in their own juices for 10 minutes.
Rinse the bulgur and add it to the pot along with 2.5 cups of water and salt. Bring to a gentle boil and cook uncovered until the liquid has almost entirely evaporated.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) and place it firmly on the pot. Steam on the lowest heat setting for 20-25 minutes until the bulgur is fluffy and the vegetables are tender.

english_name: Aromatic Spicy Kateh with Golden Chicken
description: A BOLD, ONE-POT PERSIAN RICE MASTERPIECE INFUSED WITH WARM SPICES AND BRIGHT ZEST.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion rings and sauté until they sizzle and transform into a deep, translucent gold, roughly 8 minutes.
Increase heat slightly and introduce the chicken pieces. Sear them with the onions until the edges are beautifully browned and the meat is sealed, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, curry powder, cinnamon, and black pepper. Let the spices toast for 30 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a warm, intoxicating aroma.
Add the rinsed rice to the pot along with the butter, verjuice, salt, and optional herbs. Pour in enough water to cover the rice by about one finger's width (approximately 4.5 cups).
Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce to a simmer. Once the water has been absorbed by the rice and small steam holes appear on the surface, drizzle the optional saffron liquid over the top.
Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-kan), cover tightly, and turn the heat to its lowest setting. Steam for 40 minutes to develop a perfect texture and a gentle bottom crust.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Chickpea Polo
description: A REGAL FUSION OF PROTEIN-RICH CHICKPEAS AND FRAGRANT SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot or non-stick Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Sizzle the diced onions for 8-10 minutes until they reach a beautiful, translucent golden-brown hue.
Introduce the minced garlic to the pot, sautéing for just 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with its pungent, earthy aroma.
Gently fold in the cooked chickpeas. Let them toast with the aromatics for 3 minutes to develop a slightly nutty exterior.
Stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Ensure every chickpea is coated in the warm, ochre spices to release their essential oils.
Add the washed Basmati rice to the pot. Gently toss for 2 minutes to coat the grains in the spiced oil; this prevents the rice from becoming mushy.
Pour in the bloomed saffron water for that royal glow. Add roughly 3.5 cups of water—enough to cover the rice by about two finger-widths—and give it one final, gentle stir from bottom to top.

Bring to a boil, then immediately cover with a tight-fitting lid (wrapped in a clean kitchen towel for best results) and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Steam for 25-30 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the liquid is fully absorbed.
Finish by melting the butter over the surface of the rice. Fluff gently with a fork and garnish with vibrant green parsley before serving warm.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Mixed Rice with Golden Saffron Crust
description: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN COMFORT: FLUFFY AROMATIC RICE MEETS A SHATTERING SAFFRON-YOGURT CRUST.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs crystal clear. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a heavy-bottomed skillet, sauté the diced onion in 2 tablespoons of oil until it achieves a deep golden-caramelized hue. Add the ground beef, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, and sear until beautifully browned.

Incorporate the tomato paste into the meat, frying it for 2 minutes to wake up its color and acidity. Stir in the curry powder, garlic powder, black pepper, and lemon juice. Simmer for 5 minutes until the flavors meld into a thick, aromatic ragu.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Parboil for 7-10 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain and rinse gently with lukewarm water.
Prepare the 'Golden Touch' base: Whisk the yogurt with half of your bloomed saffron and 3 tablespoons of the parboiled rice. This will create a luxurious, creamy Tahdig crust.

Pour remaining oil into the bottom of a non-stick pot. Spread the saffron-yogurt rice mixture evenly across the bottom. Layer the remaining rice, the meat ragu, diced potatoes, and dill in alternating tiers, forming a pyramid shape.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to low and steam for 35 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the bottom is a shatteringly crisp golden-brown.

english_name: Persian Tomato Rice with Succulent Lamb (Estamboli Polo)
description: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN COMFORT TALE OF TENDER RICE AND SUN-RIPENED TOMATOES.

instructions.text: Heat oil or butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat; sauté the onions until they are shimmering and translucent with a golden-brown edge.
Add the meat cubes to the pot, searing them until a rich, savory crust forms on all sides to lock in the juices.
Stir in the turmeric and tomato paste; fry the paste for 3-5 minutes until it darkens and its aroma becomes deeply concentrated.
Incorporate the chopped tomatoes and a splash of water. Cover and simmer gently on low heat until the meat is fork-tender.
Stir in the bloomed saffron (the Royal Upgrade) and season generously with salt and black pepper; the sauce should be vibrant and thick.
Rinse the Basmati rice three times until the water runs clear, then drain and fold it gently into the tomato-meat mixture.
Pour in enough water to cover the rice by about one inch and add the potato cubes, distributing them evenly.
Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce to medium heat. Cook uncovered until most of the liquid has evaporated and small steam 'craters' appear on the rice surface.
Dot the top with remaining butter. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam and create a perfect seal.
Cover tightly and steam on the lowest possible heat setting for 45 minutes to develop a crisp golden bottom (Tahdig) and fluffy grains.

english_name: Royal Saffron Estamboli Polo
description: A GOLDEN SUNSET ON YOUR PLATE: TENDER SAFFRON RICE INFUSED WITH RICH TOMATO AND CRISPY POTATO GEMS.

instructions.text: Rinse the rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 60 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, sauté the onions in oil over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until they achieve a deep, translucent gold and a sweet aroma.
Add the minced meat to the onions. Season with salt and pepper, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon. Brown the meat for 8 minutes until sizzling and fully cooked.
Incorporate the tomato paste and sauté for 2 minutes to release its deep red pigment. Add the finely chopped tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until they break down into a thick, concentrated sauce.
In a separate skillet, fry the potato cubes in oil until they are crispy and golden-brown. This ensures they maintain their integrity within the rice. Drain and stir them into the meat mixture.
Drain the soaked rice. In a large pot, combine the rice, the meat and tomato mixture, the beef broth, and the bloomed Saffron. The liquid should just barely cover the rice.

Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and cover tightly. Steam for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and a golden crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom.

english_name: Persian Tomato Rice with Tender Beef (Eslamboli Polo)
description: A RUBY-RED MASTERPIECE OF VELVETY TOMATO INFUSED RICE AND SUCCULENT SPICED BEEF.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water 3-5 times until the water runs crystal clear to ensure fluffy, non-sticky grains.

Pulse the fresh tomatoes in a blender to create a juice. Combine this juice with 3 cups of water and pour over the rice in a large pot. The liquid should sit roughly four finger-widths above the rice. Stir in 1 tbsp salt and 4 tbsp oil; let it soak for 60 minutes.

In a separate pan, sear the diced meat with the fried onions over medium-high heat until browned on all sides. Pour in 3 cups of water, cover, and simmer gently for 75 minutes until the meat is meltingly tender.
Once the meat is tender, stir in the tomato paste, pepper, and a pinch of salt. Continue to simmer uncovered until the liquid has evaporated, leaving a thick, rich meat concentrate.
Place the rice pot over medium heat. Bring to a boil and cook until the tomato liquid has been fully absorbed by the rice. If the grains still feel hard, add a splash more tomato juice.

Create a well in the center of the rice and nestle the meat mixture inside. Cover the meat with the surrounding rice. If using the 'Royal Upgrade,' drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer of rice now.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (to trap steam) and seal tightly. Cook on low heat for 60 minutes to develop the golden Tahdig crust at the bottom.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald Vegetable Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT TAPESTRY OF FRESH GARDEN VEGETABLES AND FLUFFY AROMATIC RICE INFUSED WITH WARM CUMIN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water at least 3 times until the water runs clear. In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the rice and sauté for 3-4 minutes, stirring gently until the grains are coated and smell nutty.
Pour in the chicken stock and increase the heat to high. Bring the mixture to a vigorous boil, allowing the rice to dance in the liquid.
Once boiling, stir in the diced onion, green bell pepper, chili, and tomato. Reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a steady simmer.
Simmer uncovered until most of the liquid is absorbed and small steam vents (holes) appear on the surface of the rice. At this stage, gently fold in the ground cumin, salt, and pepper.

Fold in the fresh garlic and chopped cilantro. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (the Persian 'Damkani' method) to trap steam, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest possible heat setting for a fluffy, perfect finish.

english_name: Silk Road Aromatic Vegetable Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT MEDLEY OF FRAGRANT GRAINS AND JEWEL-TONED VEGETABLES INFUSED WITH THE ESSENCE OF THE SILK ROAD.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch washes away and the water runs clear. Soak the grains in lukewarm water for 30 minutes to ensure maximum elongation.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a pungent, heavenly aroma.
Incorporate the vegetable medley into the pot. Sauté for 4 minutes until they are vibrant and slightly tender but still retain a sophisticated crunch.
Drain the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot. Gently stir for 2 minutes, allowing the grains to toast slightly and become coated in the aromatic oils.
Drizzle in the soy sauce and toasted sesame oil, stirring gently to distribute the umami flavors throughout the mixture.

Pour in the water and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a rolling boil, then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and steam for 18 minutes until the water is fully absorbed and the grains are fluffy.
For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle your bloomed saffron over a small section of the rice. Let it sit covered for 2 minutes, then fluff the entire pot with a fork, garnish with scallions, and serve.

english_name: Royal Lamb & Golden Raisin Pilaf (Keshmesh Polo)
description: SLOW-COOKED LAMB RIBS HIDDEN UNDER A FRAGRANT BLANKET OF GOLDEN RICE AND SUN-KISSED RAISINS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the starch washes away and the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside with a firm bite in the center. Drain and set aside.

In a skillet, sauté the onions in a tablespoon of oil until they reach a deep translucent gold. Toss in the raisins and sauté for only 30-60 seconds until they plump up; remove immediately to prevent burning.

Prepare your 'Dig' (pot): Coat the bottom with oil. Lay the flatbread across the base to form the crust (Tahdig). Arrange the raw lamb ribs in a single layer over the bread, seasoning them lightly with salt and a touch of the spice mix.

Layering the flavor: Spread one-third of the parboiled rice over the ribs. Top with the diced tomatoes and half of the sautéed onions and spices (turmeric, pepper, garlic, sumac, cumin). Repeat the layers, finishing with a final blanket of rice.
Scatter the plumped raisins over the top layer of rice. If using the 'Golden Touch,' drizzle saffron-infused water over the surface for a royal aroma.

Cover the pot with a tight lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel to trap the steam. Cook on the lowest possible heat for 3.5 to 4 hours. This slow-braising technique allows the lamb fats to melt into the rice while the meat becomes fork-tender.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Curry Rice with the Golden Saffron Touch
description: AN EXQUISITE FUSION OF EARTHY SILK ROAD SPICES AND ROYAL PERSIAN SAFFRON GOLD.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice in lukewarm water until the starch runs clear, then soak in heavily salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, elegant grains.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the exterior is tender but the core remains firm (al dente); drain and rinse gently with cool water.

In a large mixing bowl, delicately fold together the shredded chicken, green peas, sautéed mushrooms, half of the curry powder, and 2 tablespoons of the Royal Saffron solution until beautifully coated.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Create a 'Tahdig' base by layering thin potato slices or a portion of the parboiled rice at the bottom.
Begin layering by adding a layer of rice, followed by the aromatic chicken and vegetable mixture. Sprinkle a dusting of curry powder and a drizzle of saffron between each layer.
Whisk the remaining saffron and curry powder into the melted butter and chicken broth; pour this 'liquid gold' evenly over the top of the rice mound.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes until a steam cloud forms, then reduce to low or bake in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 60 minutes.
Gently fluff the rice and transfer to a grand platter. Crown the dish with the crunchy Tahdig pieces and a generous border of crispy golden fried potatoes.

english_name: Royal Qazvini Jeweled Rice (Nesar Polo)
description: A ROYAL MOSAIC OF SAFFRON-STAINED RICE, RUBY BARBERRIES, AND SUCCULENT MEAT.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in lukewarm salted water for 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt 1 tablespoon of ghee. Sauté the onions until translucent, then add the meat. Season with turmeric, salt, and pepper. Sear the meat for 8-10 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms.
Add a splash of water to the meat, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes (for lamb) or 20 minutes (for chicken) until the protein is fork-tender and succulent.

While the meat simmers, parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 6-8 minutes. Drain when the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite at the core.
Soak the slivered almonds and pistachios in rosewater for 15 minutes. This softens the texture and perfumes the nuts with an ancestral floral aroma.
In a pot, add a layer of ghee. Begin layering the parboiled rice, followed by spoonfuls of the meat, barberries, and the rosewater-soaked nuts. Repeat until a pyramid shape is formed.

The Golden Touch: Drizzle the bloomed saffron and remaining melted ghee over the rice. Cover with a kitchen towel-wrapped lid and steam on the lowest heat for 45 minutes to develop a crispy tahdig crust.
Gently fluff the aromatic rice and serve on a large platter, ensuring the meat and jewels of nuts and berries are beautifully distributed. Garnish with an extra pinch of saffron rice on top.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Garden Polow with Golden Saffron Chicken
description: A VIBRANT HARVEST OF GARDEN VEGETABLES AND GOLDEN SAFFRON CHICKEN LAYERED IN FLUFFY PERSIAN RICE.

instructions.text: In a glass bowl, massage the chicken cubes with the grated onion, salt, and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 180 minutes to allow the onion enzymes to tenderize the meat to perfection.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté the marinated chicken until it develops a gorgeous golden-brown crust and is cooked through, roughly 10 minutes.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the rinsed rice and parboil for 7-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center, then drain in a fine-mesh strainer.
In your pot, create a beautiful mosaic by layering the parboiled rice with the sautéed chicken, mushrooms, bell peppers, corn, and peas.
Evenly sprinkle the toasted sesame seeds between the layers for a subtle, nutty crunch in every bite.
Drizzle the 'Royal Upgrade' bloomed saffron and a touch more oil over the top. Cover with a wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and aromatic.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Herb & Green Bean Rice (Sabzi Loobia Polo)
description: A VIBRANT EMERALD MASTERPIECE OF FLUFFY BASMATI, CRISP GREEN BEANS, AND ROYAL SAFFRON-GLAZED CHICKEN.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. To build the layers of flavor, add a thin layer of rice, then a handful of green beans, a sprinkle of the vibrant chopped herbs, and a touch of fried onions. Repeat this layering process until all ingredients are used, forming a pyramid shape.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and seal tightly. Cook on medium-low heat for 40-45 minutes. This 'Dam' process allows the rice to steam perfectly while creating a crispy golden crust at the bottom.

While the rice steams, heat the remaining oil in a skillet. Sizzle the shredded chicken with tomato paste, salt, and pepper. For the 'Royal Upgrade,' pour in the bloomed saffron. Sauté for 10 minutes until the chicken is glazed in a deep crimson-gold hue and the aroma fills your kitchen.

Gently fluff the rice with a fork, ensuring the herbs and beans are evenly distributed. Mound the rice on a platter, top with the saffron-infused chicken, and serve immediately with the crunchy bottom crust (Tahdig) on the side.

english_name: Aromatic Royal Sheep's Head & Trotter Pilaf
description: A LUXURIOUS, COLLAGEN-RICH MASTERPIECE WHERE TENDER LAMB MEETS THE TANGY ALLURE OF BLACK KASHK AND SUN-DRIED FRUITS.

instructions.text: Slow-cook the sheep's head and trotters with onions and spices for 6-8 hours until the meat is incredibly tender and falling off the bone; reserve one cup of the rich, collagen-packed broth.
Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-10 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but firm in the middle (al dente); drain and rinse with cold water.
In a pan, melt 30g of butter and gently sauté the dried plums and apricots for 3-5 minutes until they are plump, glazed, and aromatic; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the minced garlic in the remaining butter until fragrant and pale gold. Stir in the water mint, golpar, and the reserved sheep broth. Simmer for 2 minutes to meld the flavors.

Layering: In a non-stick pot, add a splash of oil and a thin layer of rice. Drizzle a little Ghare-Ghoroot over the rice. Add half of the rice, then place the sautéed fruits in the center layer and drizzle more Ghare-Ghoroot.

Cover the fruit layer completely with the remaining rice. Place the succulent pieces of sheep meat and trotters on top of the rice mound. If using Saffron, drizzle the bloomed golden liquid over the meat now.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), cover the pot tightly, and steam on low heat for 45-60 minutes until a crispy golden crust (Tahdig) forms and the meat is infused with the herbal steam.

english_name: Royal Aromatic Milk Rice with Saffron and Toasted Nuts
description: A LUXURIOUS VELVET CLOUD OF SAFFRON-INFUSED RICE, SIMMERED IN CREAMY MILK AND CROWNED WITH JEWELED NUTS.

instructions.text: Drain the soaked rice thoroughly. In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, melt the butter over medium heat until it begins to foam and release a nutty aroma.
Add the drained rice to the pot and gently sauté in the butter for 3 minutes. This 'Toasted Pearl' technique coats each grain in fat, ensuring they remain distinct and fluffy rather than mushy.
Pour in the warmed milk, the bloomed saffron liquid, and sea salt. Bring to a very gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously, as milk can easily scorch the bottom of the pot.

Reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover with a lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to capture steam. Let it steam gently for 25-30 minutes until the milk is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Once the rice is cooked, sprinkle the sugar and rosewater over the surface. Gently fluff with a fork to incorporate the sweetness and floral notes without breaking the long grains.
In a separate small pan, lightly toast the slivered almonds and pistachios in a tiny pat of butter for 60 seconds until fragrant.
Transfer the golden rice to a ceremonial platter, crowning it with the toasted nuts and a few dried rose petals. Allow to rest for 5 minutes before serving to let the aromas settle.

english_name: Sardi Polo: The Silk Road Aromatic Rice
description: A GOLDEN MEDLEY OF EARTHY CUMIN, SUN-KISSED CARROTS, AND TENDER SPICED MEAT.

instructions.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a splash of oil. Add the ground meat, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, and sauté for 8-10 minutes until deeply browned and sizzling.

Stir in the crispy fried onions. Lower the heat and add the cinnamon, black cumin, green cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Bloom the spices in the meat fat for 3 minutes until the aroma fills your kitchen.

In a separate pan, combine julienned carrots with a splash of water. Cover and steam for 5 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove the lid, add a knob of butter and the raisins, and sauté for 5 more minutes until the carrots glisten and the raisins plump up.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, drizzle oil and a touch of the bloomed saffron if using. Layer the parboiled rice with the spiced meat and the carrot-raisin mixture. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to develop a golden crust (Tahdig).

english_name: Persian Tomato Rice with Crispy Potato Tahdig
description: A CRIMSON CLOUD OF AROMATIC RICE CROWNED WITH A SHATTERING GOLDEN POTATO CRUST.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water several times until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in salted water for 15 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
In a medium pot, bring 3 cups of water to a simmer. Dissolve the bouillon cubes into the water, ensuring no lumps remain, to create a savory foundation.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a small pan. Sauté the tomato paste for 3 minutes until it turns a deep, dark crimson and smells fragrant. Stir in the tomato juice and bring to a light boil.

Add the drained rice and the tomato mixture into the simmering broth. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is mostly absorbed by the rice grains but they are still 'al dente'.
In a separate non-stick pot, melt half the butter. Arrange the potato slices in a single layer at the bottom. This will become your 'Tahdig'—the legendary golden crust.

Gently spoon the par-cooked tomato rice over the potatoes, shaping it into a pyramid. Poke 3-4 holes into the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape. Pour the remaining melted butter and the optional Saffron bloom over the top for a Royal Touch.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap steam. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat possible for 35-45 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the potato crust is shattering and golden.

english_name: Silk Road Golden Chicken & Rice Medley
description: A RADIANT HARMONY OF TENDER CHICKEN AND AROMATIC RICE INFUSED WITH THE COLORS OF THE SILK ROAD.

instructions.text: Melt the butter or ghee in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onions for 8 to 10 minutes until they achieve a deep, translucent amber glow and a sweet aroma.
Increase the heat slightly and add the chicken cubes. Sear the chicken for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the edges are golden-brown and the juices are sealed inside.
Incorporate the chopped tomatoes, scallions, and the primary diced bell pepper. Allow them to soften and sizzle for 5 minutes, creating a rustic, colorful base for the rice.
Add the turmeric and the tricolor bell pepper mince. Season generously with salt and pepper, stirring to coat every ingredient in the aromatic golden oils.
Gently fold in the cooked rice. If using the 'Royal Upgrade,' drizzle the bloomed saffron over the rice now. Toss gently for 4 minutes until the rice is heated through and brilliantly colored.
Turn off the heat. Sprinkle the fresh basil chiffonade over the dish and finish with a bright splash of fresh lemon juice for a zesty, elevated lift.

english_name: Persian Lamb Neck Stew with Aromatic Steamed Rice
description: EXPERIENCE THE VELVETY PERFECTION OF LAMB NECK SLOW-STEAMED TO BONE-FALLING TENDERNESS.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté onions over medium heat for about 12 minutes until they reach a deep, golden-brown caramelization.
Add the lamb neck to the pot, searing it on all sides until it develops a rich brown crust and mingles with the sweetness of the onions.
Stir in the tomato paste and sauté for 3 minutes until the oil turns a vibrant red and the raw metallic scent of the paste vanishes.
Pour in the bloomed saffron and salt, then add 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 90 minutes.
While the meat simmers, parboil your Basmati rice in salted water for 7 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but firm in the middle; drain and rinse with cold water.
In a clean, large pot, create a bed of half the parboiled rice. Place the semi-cooked lamb neck and its concentrated juices in the center, then cover with the remaining rice.
Dust the top with ground cinnamon. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on the lowest heat for 120 minutes, allowing the rice steam to finish cooking the lamb to perfection.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin of Shiraz
description: A SYMPHONY OF CRUNCH AND SILK: THE GOLDEN CROWN OF PERSIAN CUISINE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice repeatedly until the water runs crystal clear. Soak in salted lukewarm water for at least 2 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, parboil the rice until the exterior is soft but the core still retains a firm bite (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking process.

Whisk the eggs and the extra yolk until smooth. Fold in the thick yogurt, half of your bloomed Saffron liquid, and a pinch of salt. Gently mix this golden custard with the parboiled rice until every grain is coated in sunshine.
Sauté the diced onion in a pan with a splash of oil until translucent and golden. Add the shredded chicken, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Sizzle for 5 minutes until the aromas fill your kitchen.

Generously oil a glass or non-stick baking dish. Press half of the saffron rice firmly into the bottom. Layer the savory chicken mixture in the center, leaving a small border, then crown it with the remaining rice, smoothing the surface with a spatula.

Seal the dish tightly with aluminum foil. Place in a preheated oven at 200°C (390°F) for 30 minutes to set the structure, then reduce to 160°C (320°F) for 15 minutes to develop the legendary crisp crust.
While the rice rests, sauté the barberries and almond slivers in butter with the remaining saffron and a pinch of sugar for 2 minutes until they glisten like rubies.
Invert the Tahchin onto a platter. The 'thud' of the crust releasing is music to a chef's ears. Garnish with the jeweled barberries and almonds.

english_name: Royal Golden Saffron & Spinach Tahchin Cake
description: THE CROWN JEWEL OF PERSIAN CUISINE: A CRISPY, GOLDEN SAFFRON CRUST REVEALING A VIBRANT SPINACH AND JEWELED CENTER.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water.
Bloom your saffron: Place crushed saffron in a small bowl with a single ice cube; let it melt to extract a deep, royal crimson hue.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt, eggs, half of the bloomed saffron, and 2 tablespoons of oil. Season with salt. Gently fold in half of the parboiled rice until every grain is coated in the golden velvet mixture.
Sauté the barberries and pistachios in a small pan with a teaspoon of butter and the sugar for 2 minutes until they glisten and swell. Set aside a spoonful for garnish.

Generously coat the bottom and sides of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot or glass baking dish with oil and melted butter. Spread the saffron-yogurt rice across the bottom, pressing firmly with a spatula to create the foundation for your crust.
Layer the sautéed barberries and pistachios over the rice, followed by the shredded meat (if using). Add the sautéed spinach as the next vibrant green layer.
Mix the remaining white rice with the rest of the yogurt and saffron, then layer it on top. Press down firmly to compact the 'cake'. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake in a preheated oven at 360°F (180°C) for 90 to 120 minutes. You are looking for a deep, honeycomb-golden crust to form on the sides and bottom.
Allow to rest for 10 minutes before flipping onto a platter. The 'tahdig' should release with a satisfying 'thud'. Garnish with the reserved barberries and pistachios.

english_name: Royal Saffron Rice Cake with Velvet Eggplant & Chicken
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CRUST HIDING A HEART OF VELVET EGGPLANT AND TENDER SAFFRON CHICKEN.

instructions.text: Parboil the washed Basmati rice in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water for 7-8 minutes. The grains should be al dente—soft on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks with a pinch of salt and pepper until pale. Incorporate the thick yogurt, half the oil, and the 'Royal Upgrade'—our vibrant saffron liquid. The mixture should be a deep, sun-kissed orange.
Gently fold the parboiled rice into the saffron-yogurt mixture until every grain is coated in the golden velvet. This ensures the signature creamy-yet-firm interior of the Tahchin.
Generously oil a deep non-stick baking dish or a glass Pyrex. Spread half of the saffron rice across the bottom, pressing down firmly with a spatula to create a compact base.

Layer the fried eggplant slices and the shredded chicken evenly over the rice. Season this middle layer lightly with pepper. Cover with the remaining saffron rice, smoothing and pressing the top to seal the treasures inside.

Cover the dish tightly with foil and pierce a few steam vents with a fork. Bake in a preheated oven at 175°C (347°F) for 90 minutes. You are looking for a deep, crunchy crust—the legendary Tahdig—to form on the bottom and sides.
While the rice bakes, melt butter in a pan and quickly sauté the barberries with a teaspoon of sugar for 2 minutes until they glisten like rubies. Do not overcook or they will turn bitter.

The Grand Finale: Remove the foil, place a large platter over the dish, and confidently invert it. The Tahchin should emerge as a monolithic golden cake. Garnish with the buttered barberries and serve in slices.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin with Walnuts and Barberries
description: A GOLDEN SPECTACLE OF CRISPY SAFFRON RICE BURSTING WITH JEWELED BARBERRIES AND ROASTED WALNUTS.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed skillet, heat the oil over medium heat. Sauté the pre-fried caramelized onions for 1 minute to release their aroma, then add the ground lamb. Break the meat apart with a spoon and sear until it develops a deep, savory brown color.

Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Add the chopped walnuts and barberries, folding them into the meat. Pour in half of the bloomed saffron liquid. Cover and let the flavors meld on low heat for 10 minutes until the meat is tender and the barberries are plump.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the yogurt, 4 egg yolks, the whole egg, and the remaining bloomed saffron until the mixture is a vibrant, uniform gold. Gently fold the parboiled rice into this velvety golden custard until every grain is perfectly coated.

Generously grease a non-stick ovenproof glass dish or heavy pan with butter. Spread half of the golden rice mixture across the bottom, pressing firmly with the back of a spoon to create a solid base for the crust.
Distribute the meat, walnut, and barberry mixture evenly over the rice layer, leaving a small margin at the edges to prevent the filling from burning against the sides.
Top with the remaining saffron rice, smoothing the surface and pressing down gently. Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and pierce a few steam holes with a fork.
Place in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F). Bake for 90 minutes. You are looking for the sides and bottom to turn a deep, mahogany gold, visible through the glass dish.

Remove from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes. Carefully run a knife around the edges, place a serving platter over the dish, and flip with confidence. The Tahchin should emerge as a magnificent, golden rice cake.

english_name: Royal Saffron and Sour Cherry Tahchin
description: A CRUNCHY SAFFRON JEWEL BOX BURSTING WITH TART PERSIAN CHERRIES.

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the sour cherries and sugar. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes until the cherries release their juices and the syrup thickens slightly. Strain the cherries, reserving the ruby-red syrup.

Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes. The grains should be soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, egg yolks, half of the melted butter, and your bloomed saffron liquid. Gently fold in half of the parboiled rice until every grain is coated in a vibrant golden hue.
Prepare your baking dish by greasing it generously with oil and a drizzle of cherry syrup. Layer the saffron-yogurt rice at the bottom, pressing firmly with a spoon to create the base for the crust.

Layer the shredded meat (if using), caramelized onions, and the strained sour cherries over the saffron rice. Top with the remaining white rice, drizzling the rest of the melted butter and a few spoonfuls of cherry syrup over the top.
Cover the dish tightly with foil (or heat-safe wrap) and bake in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F) for 45 to 60 minutes. You are looking for a deep, golden-brown crust to form around the edges.
Allow to rest for 5 minutes, then carefully invert the dish onto a platter. The result should be a shimmering, jewel-toned rice cake with a perfectly crispy exterior.

english_name: Golden Silk Road Mushroom & Chicken Pilaf
description: A SYMPHONY OF EARTHY MUSHROOMS AND TENDER CHICKEN WRAPPED IN THE GOLDEN EMBRACE OF ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking process.

Heat oil and butter in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces, seasoning with salt and pepper, and sear for 5-7 minutes until they develop a beautiful golden-brown crust and are cooked through.
Introduce the minced garlic, grated ginger, and curry powder to the skillet. Sauté for exactly 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a warm, intoxicating aroma.
Fold in the fried onions and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 3-4 minutes on high heat, allowing the mushrooms to release their moisture and brown slightly without becoming soggy.
Add the vibrant tri-color bell peppers and drizzle in the royal saffron infusion. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until the peppers are tender-crisp and the mixture is stained a magnificent gold.
In a clean non-stick pot, layer three-quarters of the parboiled rice. Spread 5-6 tablespoons of the chicken-mushroom mixture over this layer, then top with the remaining rice.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-kesh) to trap steam. Cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes until the rice is fluffy and a steam cloud rises when the lid is lifted.
Gently fluff the rice and plate it on a grand platter. Crown the dish with the remaining mushroom-chicken mixture and a shower of fresh parsley.

english_name: Reshteh Polo: The Golden Noodle Rice with Saffron Lamb
description: A SYMPHONY OF TOASTED NOODLES AND MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH LAMB INFUSED WITH ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Place the lamb chunks in a heavy-bottomed pot with one sliced onion and a bay leaf. Cover with 8 cups of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 90 to 120 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and falling off the bone.
While the meat braises, wash the Basmati rice in cold water until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure maximum grain length.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with 1 tablespoon of salt. Add the soaked rice and boil for about 5 minutes. Then, add the toasted noodles to the boiling water with the rice for the final 5 minutes of parboiling.
Drain the rice and noodles in a fine-mesh colander and rinse briefly with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process.

Coat the bottom of your pot with oil. For a luxury touch, place a layer of thin bread or sliced potatoes to create a 'Tahdig' crust. Mound the rice and noodle mixture into the pot in a pyramid shape. Poke holes with a spoon handle to allow steam to escape.
Drizzle a mixture of warm water and oil over the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on low heat for 60 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the bottom is crispy.

In a separate pan, sauté the remaining sliced onion in oil until deeply golden and caramelized. Add turmeric and the cooked lamb chunks, searing them until they sizzle. Season with salt and half of the bloomed saffron.

To serve, spread the noodle rice on a platter, nestle the succulent lamb in the center, and drizzle with the remaining saffron-infused lamb broth. Garnish with the extra saffron rice for a royal finish.

english_name: Persian Golden Chickpea Rice (Nokhod Polo)
description: A GOLDEN TAPESTRY OF FLUFFY BASMATI RICE, BUTTERY CHICKPEAS, AND THE ROYAL GLOW OF SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the starch runs clear. Soak in cold water with 2 tablespoons of sea salt for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Simmer the chickpeas in salted water for 5 minutes to refresh their texture, then drain and set aside.
In a non-stick pan, fry the potato cubes in a drizzle of oil until they develop a crisp, golden-brown exterior. Remove and set aside to keep them from softening.
In a large pot, sauté the julienned onions with turmeric in oil until they are caramelized and fragrant.
Pour the pureed tomatoes into the pot with the onions. Increase the heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until the water evaporates and you are left with a thick, concentrated crimson sauce.
Add 4 cups of water, salt, and a splash of oil to the tomato base. Bring to a rolling boil, then stir in the chickpeas.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling liquid. Let it cook uncovered until the water reduces by half. Gently fold in the crispy potatoes and drizzle the bloomed saffron over the surface.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap the steam. Cover tightly, reduce heat to the lowest setting, and allow the rice to steam into fluffy perfection for 60 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork, transfer to a platter, and garnish with fresh parsley for a burst of color and earthiness.

english_name: Silk Road Seasonal Harvest Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT TAPESTRY OF SEASONAL VEGETABLES NESTLED IN CLOUDS OF AROMATIC SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.

Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add the cubed potatoes and sear until the edges are golden. Toss in the green beans, peas, and corn, sautéing for 8 minutes until the colors become vibrant and the edges slightly caramelized.
Incorporate the diced tomatoes, garlic powder, cinnamon, pepper, and turmeric. Allow the spices to bloom in the hot oil for 5 minutes, filling your kitchen with a warm, earthy aroma.
Pour in 2 cups of boiling water, reduce the heat to low, and cover. Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the liquid has transformed into a rich, concentrated sauce.

In a separate large pot, parboil the soaked rice in boiling salted water for 6-8 minutes until 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking.

Prepare the pot for steaming by adding a layer of oil and potato slices at the bottom for a 'Tahdig' crust. Layer the rice and the vegetable mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Reserve a small portion of vegetables for garnish.

For the 'Royal Upgrade', sprinkle bloomed saffron and extra cinnamon over the top layer. Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on low heat for 90 minutes until the rice is aromatic and the bottom crust is perfectly crisp.

english_name: Royal Lamb Shank with Aromatic Dill & Fava Bean Rice
description: THE CROWN JEWEL OF PERSIAN HOSPITALITY: FALL-OFF-THE-BONE LAMB PAIRED WITH EMERALD AROMATIC RICE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear. Soak in heavily salted water for at least 3 hours to ensure the grains achieve their maximum length and fluffiness.

In a heavy pot, sear the lamb shanks with half the diced onions until a deep golden crust forms. Add turmeric and 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim off any impurities, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is buttery and ready to fall off the bone.

In a large pot of boiling salted water, drop in the fava beans. If fresh, cook for 5 minutes; if frozen, give them 8 minutes. Add the drained rice to the same pot and parboil for 7 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—firm in the center but tender on the outside. Drain and rinse with lukewarm water.

Prepare the pot for 'Tahdig' by adding oil to the bottom. Carefully layer the parboiled rice and fava beans with the chopped fresh dill, building a pyramid shape. Drizzle with melted butter and half of your liquid gold saffron.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap the steam. Cook on high for 3 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 60 minutes for a perfect aromatic infusion.

While the rice steams, remove the shanks from their broth and strain the liquid. In a skillet, sauté the remaining onions until caramelized. Stir in tomato paste and turmeric, cook for 2 minutes to wake up the flavors, then return the shanks and 1 cup of the strained broth. Simmer until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy glaze.

To serve, fluff the rice gently with a fork. Plate the emerald-green rice on a platter, crown it with the remaining saffron rice, and place the majestic lamb shanks alongside, drizzled with their rich reduction.

english_name: Aromatic Golden Rice with Parmesan Cloud
description: A GOLDEN EMBRACE OF FRAGRANT RICE AND VELVETY PARMESAN CHEESE.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the finely diced onion and sauté for about 5 minutes until it becomes translucent and soft, releasing its natural sweetness without browning.
Drain the soaked rice thoroughly and add it to the pot. Stir gently for 1 minute to coat every grain in the aromatic butter, seasoning with a generous pinch of sea salt and black pepper.

Pour in the rich broth and the bloomed saffron water (the Golden Touch). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and allow the rice to absorb the liquid and steam to perfection for 25 to 30 minutes.
Once the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, remove from heat. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan over the top and fold it in with a fork using light, airy strokes to maintain the fluffiness.

english_name: Silk Road Surf & Turf Fried Rice with Miniature Spiced Koftas
description: A ROYAL EXPLOSION OF SURF, TURF, AND SPICE INSPIRED BY THE ANCIENT TRADE ROUTES.

instructions.text: In a chilled bowl, combine the ground meat, grated onion, chili powder, curry powder, and egg white. Knead the mixture vigorously for 5 minutes until it becomes tacky and smooth; this ensures the koftas stay succulent.

Shape the mixture into walnut-sized balls. Heat vegetable oil in a pan and fry the koftas for 5-6 minutes, turning frequently until they achieve a deep mahogany crust and are fully cooked. Drain on a wire rack and thread 2-3 onto mini bamboo skewers.

Whisk the 2 eggs with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. In a wide pan, heat 1 tablespoon of peanut oil and pour the egg mixture to create a thin, silk-like omelet. Remove from heat, slice one half into ribbons and finely shred the other half for garnish.

In a large wok or heavy-bottomed skillet, heat the remaining peanut oil over high heat until shimmering. Sauté the sliced onions, garlic, and both bell peppers for 3-4 minutes until softened but still vibrant.
Add the cubed chicken and beef to the wok. Season with the pepper and sear over high heat for 8-10 minutes, allowing the meat to develop a golden-brown char while remaining tender inside.
Toss in the raw shrimp and bean sprouts. Stir-fry rapidly for 3 minutes until the shrimp turn a perfect opaque pink and the sprouts just begin to wilt.

Fold in the chilled rice, the omelet ribbons, the remaining soy sauce, and the optional bloomed saffron. Use a folding motion to incorporate the flavors for 3 minutes until the rice is piping hot and takes on a golden, aromatic hue.
Garnish with fresh cilantro. To serve, mound the aromatic rice in the center of a platter, topping with the shredded egg and the kofta skewers for a grand presentation.

english_name: Silk Road Burrito: Aromatic Rice & Golden Chicken Melts
description: A LUXURIOUS FUSION WHERE ANCIENT SPICES MEET THE BOLD VIBRANCY OF THE AMERICAS.

instructions.text: In a pot of boiling salted water, parboil the rinsed rice for about 7-8 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onions for 8-10 minutes until they reach a deep translucent gold, releasing their natural sweetness.
Stir in the ground cloves and dried oregano. Toast the spices for 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a warm, earthy aroma.
Add the grated tomato pulp. Simmer gently for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has evaporated and you are left with a thick, concentrated tomato jam.
Fold the parboiled rice into the tomato mixture. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle it over the rice now for a majestic aroma and golden hue. Mix gently to coat every grain.
Poach or pan-sear the chicken until fully cooked (internal temperature 75°C/165°F), then shred into bite-sized ribbons. Incorporate the chicken and grated cheddar into the warm rice mixture.
Preheat your oven to 160°C (320°F). Wrap the tortillas in foil and steam them for 5 minutes or place in a steamer until soft and pliable.
Place a generous portion of the filling in the center of each tortilla. Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a neat parcel.
Arrange the burritos in a baking dish, cover tightly with foil to lock in moisture, and warm in the oven for 10 minutes to allow the cheese to fuse the ingredients together before serving.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Tomato & Pea Rice
description: A VIBRANT FUSION OF SUN-RIPENED TOMATOES AND SWEET PEAS WOVEN INTO FLUFFY AROMATIC GRAINS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to achieve that elegant, long-grain elongation.

In a heavy-bottomed pan, sizzle the diced onions in olive oil until they turn a beautiful translucent gold, about 8 minutes. Stir in the crushed garlic for the last 60 seconds until the kitchen is filled with a rich, savory aroma.
Pour your fresh tomato puree into the pan. Simmer over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, allowing the water to evaporate until the sauce thickens into a concentrated, vibrant crimson base.
Briefly blanch the garden peas in boiling water for 3 minutes to preserve their emerald green color and snap, then drain immediately.

Drain the rice and add it to a large pot with the boiling water and vegetable broth. Fold in the tomato reduction, golden onions, garlic, peas, dried chilies, and black pepper. This is where the magic happens—the rice begins to absorb every layer of flavor.

Bring to a gentle boil until the liquid level drops below the rice. If you desire the 'Golden Touch,' drizzle a teaspoon of bloomed saffron over the top now. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (damkani) and seal tightly.
Steam on the lowest possible heat for 30 minutes. The result will be fluffy, aromatic grains with a hint of spice and a colorful garden aesthetic.

original_name: پلوی ساده با طعم هل و میخک
english_name: Silk Road Aromatic Basmati with Cardamom & Cloves
description: A FRAGRANT CLOUD OF HEAVENLY BASMATI INFUSED WITH THE WARMTH OF THE ANCIENT SPICE TRADE.

instructions.text: Place the rice in a large bowl and rinse it gently under cold water at least 3-4 times until the water runs crystal clear. This removes excess starch to ensure every grain remains separate and fluffy.
Soak the rinsed rice in salted water for at least 30 minutes. This strengthens the grain and allows it to elongate beautifully during the cooking process.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, bring 3 cups of filtered water to a rolling boil. Drop in the cracked cardamom pods and cloves, allowing them to dance in the water for 2 minutes to release their ancient, warm essential oils.
Drain the soaking rice and carefully add it to the boiling aromatic water. Stir in the butter and salt. If using rosewater, add it now to infuse the steam with a delicate floral whisper.
Maintain a medium-high heat until the water has mostly evaporated and small 'steam chimneys' or pits appear on the surface of the rice. Do not stir during this stage.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to prevent steam from escaping or dripping back. Place the lid firmly on the pot, reduce heat to the lowest setting, and let the rice steam into perfection.
Optional Golden Touch: Before serving, drizzle your bloomed saffron over a small portion of the rice, mix, and scatter the golden grains over the platter for a royal finish.

english_name: Persian Wild Herb & Lamb Pilaf (Shang Polo)
description: A RARE SPRINGTIME DELICACY OF FORAGED WILD HERBS AND MELT-IN-YOUR-MOUTH BRAISED LAMB.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in a large bowl of salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Prepare the 'Shang' leaves by removing tough stems and finely chopping the greens. Set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat. Add the onions and sauté until they turn a deep golden-caramel brown, roughly 10-12 minutes.
Add the turmeric and half of the bloomed saffron to the onions, letting the spices toast for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the meat cubes, searing them until browned on all sides.
Pour in 1 cup of boiling water, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer the meat gently for 90 minutes until it is fork-tender and the liquid has reduced into a thick, aromatic gravy.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, add the soaked rice and the chopped Shang leaves. Boil for 7-8 minutes until the rice is 'al dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside.
Drain the rice and herbs in a fine-mesh colander, rinsing quickly with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process.
To create the Tahdig, wipe the rice pot clean, add 2 tablespoons of oil and a splash of the remaining saffron water. Arrange the potato slices in a single layer at the bottom.

Gently mound the rice and herb mixture over the potatoes. Poke a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape. Cover with a lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (damkoni) and steam on low heat for 45 minutes.
Platter the fluffy green rice, topping it with the succulent braised meat and the crispy potato Tahdig on the side.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Dill and Broad Bean Rice (Baghali Polo)
description: A VIBRANT, JEWELED MASTERPIECE OF FRAGRANT DILL AND BUTTERY BROAD BEANS INFUSED WITH THE SCENT OF ANCIENT PERSIA.

instructions.text: In a large pot, bring 3 cups of water and a generous pinch of salt to a rolling boil. Add the washed Basmati rice and parboil for exactly 10 minutes. The grains should be soft on the outside but still firm to the bite (al dente). Drain the rice in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse quickly with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process.

Melt one-third of the butter in a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot over low heat. To build the foundation of your Tahdig (the golden crust), spread a thin layer of parboiled rice across the bottom. Layer one-quarter of the broad beans and a handful of chopped dill over the rice.

Continue building the masterpiece by alternating layers of rice, broad beans, and dill in a pyramid shape. Ensure the final top layer is plain rice. Pour half a small glass of water around the edges of the pot to create steam, cover tightly, and cook on medium-high heat for 8 minutes until steam begins to form.

Melt the remaining butter and drizzle it evenly over the rice. Sprinkle the ground cinnamon, cumin, and red pepper flakes across the top. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap every drop of moisture, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and let it steam gently for 30 minutes until fluffy and aromatic.

For the 'Golden Touch,' take a spoonful of the cooked rice and mix it with your bloomed saffron liquid. Gently fluff the rest of the rice onto a platter, top with the vibrant saffron-infused rice, and garnish with fresh dill sprigs for a royal presentation.

english_name: Persian Jeweled Pilaf with Saffron Meatballs (Chashm-Bolboli Polo)
description: A ROYAL TAPESTRY OF FLUFFY SAFFRON RICE, EARTHY PEAS, AND SUCCULENT MINI-MEATBALLS THAT DEFINES PERSIAN ELEGANCE.

instructions.text: Rinse the black-eyed peas thoroughly and soak for at least 2 hours. Drain and simmer in a pot of salted water for 25-30 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain and set aside.

In a large skillet, sauté two of the diced onions in olive oil over medium heat until they turn a deep translucent gold. Stir in 1 teaspoon of turmeric and the cooked peas, tossing gently to infuse the earthy aromas.
Parboil the pre-soaked rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside with a firm bite in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, drizzle oil and a splash of water. Layer the rice and the pea-onion mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes in the rice to let steam escape, cover with a cloth-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 45 minutes.

While the rice steams, prepare the 'Kofteh-Rizeh'. Mix the ground meat with the remaining onion, minced garlic, salt, pepper, and tomato paste. Roll into marble-sized meatballs and sear in a hot pan with butter until browned and succulent.

The Royal Upgrade: Grind your saffron with a pinch of sugar and bloom it in two tablespoons of hot water. Melt butter and mix with the saffron liquid, then drizzle this liquid gold over the fluffy rice before serving.
Plate the aromatic rice on a large platter, arrange the glistening meatballs around the edges, and garnish generously with fresh parsley for a burst of color and zest.

english_name: Royal Persian Spinach and Saffron Rice Cake (Tahchin Esfenaj)
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CRUST HIDING A TREASURE OF SAVORY SPINACH AND AROMATIC SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.

In a medium pan, sauté half of the onions in olive oil until translucent and golden. Add the chopped spinach and a pinch of salt, sautéing for 5-7 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the spinach is fragrant and tender. Set aside.
