Grate the remaining onion and mix it with the ground meat. Brown the meat in a hot pan with olive oil, seasoning with salt, pepper, and one tablespoon of your liquid saffron 'Royal Upgrade'. Sauté for 10 minutes until the meat is fully browned and juices are absorbed.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Drain the soaked rice and parboil for about 6-8 minutes. The grains should be 'al dente'—soft on the outside but still firm in the middle. Drain and rinse briefly with cool water.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks, yogurt, and the remaining bloomed saffron until smooth and vibrant orange. Gently fold the parboiled rice into this mixture until every grain is coated in the golden velvet.

Coat a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot with oil. Layer half the saffron rice, pressing down slightly. Spread the spinach mixture, then the meat mixture as even layers. Top with the remaining rice. Dot with butter cubes. Cover with a lid wrapped in a kitchen towel and steam on the lowest heat for 90-120 minutes until a deep golden crust (Tahdig) forms. Invert onto a platter to serve.

english_name: Royal Saffron Chicken Tahchin
description: THE CROWN JEWEL OF PERSIAN CUISINE: A FRAGRANT, CRISPY SAFFRON RICE CAKE THAT REVEALS TENDER MERINGUE-LIKE LAYERS WITHIN.

instructions.text: Place the chicken in a pot with the onion, turmeric, salt, and enough water to cover. Simmer gently for 45-50 minutes until tender. Once cooked, ensure about 1/2 cup of concentrated broth remains. Shred the chicken into large, succulent chunks, removing all bones.

In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, 4 egg yolks, 3/4 of the bloomed saffron, salt, and pepper. Fold the chicken pieces into this golden mixture and refrigerate for at least 3-4 hours to allow the flavors to penetrate the fibers.

Par-boil the rinsed rice in salted boiling water for 6-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still firm (al dente) in the center. Drain and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process.

In a separate bowl, mix 3 cups of the par-boiled rice with the remaining 2 egg yolks, 150g of oil, and half of the leftover yogurt marinade. Spread this mixture firmly into the bottom of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot to create the foundation for the golden crust.

Layer half of the marinated chicken over the rice base, followed by a layer of plain rice. Repeat with the remaining chicken and top with the final layer of rice. Press down firmly with a spatula to compact the 'cake'.

Mix the reserved chicken broth with the remaining saffron and drizzle evenly over the rice. Pour the remaining melted oil over the top. Cover with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a kitchen towel (Damkoni) and cook on low-medium heat for 90 minutes until a thick, golden crust forms.

The moment of truth: Place a large serving platter over the pot and swiftly invert it. The Tahchin should emerge as a magnificent, shimmering golden-brown cake. Garnish with barberries or pistachios if desired.

english_name: Golden Harvest Lentil and Carrot Dami
description: A SUN-KISSED ONE-POT WONDER BLENDING EARTHY LENTILS WITH CARAMELIZED CARROT SWEETNESS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the turmeric and stir for 30 seconds until it blooms and turns the oil a vibrant gold.
Add the finely chopped onion to the golden oil. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until the onions are translucent and slightly caramelized at the edges.

Incorporate the lentils and a pinch of salt. Pour in enough water to cover the lentils by an inch, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until par-cooked but still holding their shape.
Add the diced carrots and tomato paste to the pot. Stir well to coat everything in the aromatic base, cooking for another 5 minutes until the carrots begin to soften.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot along with the Persian Advieh. Pour in the 3 cups of water (or enough to cover the rice by half an inch). Adjust salt as needed.

Bring to a vigorous boil until the water has mostly evaporated and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface of the rice. Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), cover tightly, and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Steam for 35-40 minutes to develop a crisp bottom crust.
For a Royal Upgrade, drizzle your bloomed saffron over the top of the rice before serving. Fluff gently with a fork, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve with yogurt or pickled vegetables.

english_name: Silk Road Aromatic Pepper & Golden Chicken Rice
description: A KALEIDOSCOPE OF VIBRANT PEPPERS AND TENDER CHICKEN INFUSED WITH THE ROYAL GLOW OF SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, sizzle the onions in olive oil until translucent. Add the chicken medallions, searing them over medium-high heat until a beautiful golden-brown crust forms. Stir in the garlic, turmeric, cumin, and coriander, allowing the spices to bloom and release their intoxicating aroma for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and half of your saffron water. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and let the chicken poach for 15-20 minutes until tender and the liquid is rich with essence.
In a separate pan, flash-sauté the bell peppers with a pinch of salt for 3 minutes. You want them vibrant and slightly softened, not mushy. Set them aside.

Drain the soaked rice and add it directly into the pot with the chicken and simmering stock. The liquid should cover the rice by about one centimeter. Increase heat to high until the liquid boils off and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface of the rice.

Gently fold the sautéed peppers and the remaining saffron water into the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani), place it firmly on the pot, and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Let it steam perfectly for 25-30 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork to release the steam, garnish generously with fresh cilantro, and serve with a side of yogurt.

english_name: Aromatic Tarragon Pan-Kebab (Kabab-e-Tarkhouni)
description: THE SOPHISTICATED PERSIAN KEBAB UPGRADE INFUSED WITH ROYAL AROMATIC TARRAGON.

instructions.text: Prepare the aromatic heart of the dish by washing and thoroughly drying the tarragon. Finely mince the leaves to release their signature anise-like oils.

Grate the onion using the fine side of a box grater. This is the secret step: wrap the pulp in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze hard to remove every drop of excess liquid, leaving only the concentrated onion essence.
In a large chilled mixing bowl, combine the meat, squeezed onion pulp, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Use your hands to incorporate the spices evenly through the protein.
Fold in the minced tarragon and knead the mixture for at least 5 minutes. This creates a bouncy, professional texture that ensures the kebabs hold their shape without breaking.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Shape the meat into small elongated logs or flat patties. Sear until a deep, caramelized mahogany crust forms, about 4-5 minutes per side.

Steam your Basmati rice until fluffy. For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the ice-bloomed saffron over the top layer of rice and finish with a knob of melting butter. Serve the sizzling kebabs alongside the golden rice.

english_name: Traditional Persian Adas Polo with Saffron-Infused Chicken
description: A SYMPHONY OF FRAGRANT BASMATI, EARTHY LENTILS, AND TENDER SAFFRON-KISSED CHICKEN.

instructions.text: Rinse the lentils thoroughly and simmer in a pot with water for about 20-25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. Drain and set aside.

In a heavy-bottomed pan, sauté the diced onions in oil until they reach a deep golden-brown caramelization. Add the cubed chicken and sear until the exterior is beautifully browned and the aroma fills the kitchen.
Introduce the diced bell peppers to the chicken mixture. Season with salt and pepper, stirring gently for 5 minutes until the peppers soften and the flavors meld into a savory sauce.
Parboil the pre-soaked rice in heavily salted boiling water for 7-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but firm in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a large non-stick pot, add a layer of oil and a splash of bloomed saffron. Layer the parboiled rice, cooked lentils, and the chicken-pepper mixture in a pyramid shape. Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to create a crispy Tahdig.
Quickly toast the slivered almonds in a teaspoon of oil until fragrant. Garnish the fluffy rice with the almonds and the remaining Golden Touch saffron for a royal presentation.

english_name: Aromatic Emerald & Gold Spinach Rice (Esfenaj Polo)
description: A VIBRANT EMERALD MASTERPIECE OF SILKY SPINACH AND FRAGRANT SAFFRON-KISSED RICE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Place the fresh spinach in a wide pan over medium heat. Sauté without oil until the moisture has evaporated and the leaves have wilted into a deep emerald concentrate.

In a separate skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with olive oil. Sauté the grated onion and garlic with turmeric until they reach a shimmering golden hue and the kitchen is filled with a sweet, toasted aroma.
Stir the wilted spinach into the onion mixture. Season generously with salt, pepper, and a splash of lemon juice to brighten the earthy tones. Sauté for 2 minutes and set aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the center. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Coat the bottom of a non-stick pot with oil. Lay the bread across the bottom to create the legendary Tahdig crust. Layer the rice and the spinach mixture alternately, forming a pyramid shape.
Make holes in the rice with the back of a spoon to let steam escape. Drizzle with melted butter and 1/4 cup water. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel, seal tightly, and steam on low heat for 45 minutes.
For the Royal Finish, take a cup of the cooked white rice, mix it with your bloomed saffron, and use it to garnish the top of the dish before serving.

english_name: Royal Persian Red Bean Jewel Rice
description: A VELVETY SYMPHONY OF EARTHY BEANS AND FRAGRANT RICE, ELEVATED BY THE ROYAL TOUCH OF SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the red kidney beans thoroughly and soak in cold water for 24 hours to ensure a velvety texture and easy digestion, changing the water once.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium-low heat. Sauté the onions and garlic for 6 minutes until they become translucent and start to release their sweet aroma.
If using lamb or sausage, increase the heat to medium and sear the meat along with thyme and chili flakes for 5 minutes until beautifully browned and fragrant.
Drain the soaked beans and add them to the pot with 4 cups of water. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer covered for 90 minutes until the beans are tender but still hold their shape.
Stir in the tomato paste, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Let the mixture simmer for another 10 minutes to allow the flavors to deepen and the sauce to thicken slightly.

In a separate pot, parboil your Basmati rice in salted water for 7 minutes until the grains are long and tender on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

Layer the parboiled rice and the red bean mixture in a pot. If using the 'Golden Touch', drizzle your bloomed saffron over the top layer. Cover and steam on low heat for 10 minutes to marry the flavors.

english_name: Royal Ghabooli: The Silk Road Spiced Lamb & Chickpea Pilaf
description: A SPICED CULINARY VOYAGE OF TENDER LAMB, HONEYED DATES, AND AROMATIC SILK ROAD SPICES.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot, combine the lamb, soaked chickpeas, and the halved raw onion. Cover with water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 90 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and chickpeas are soft but holding their shape.
Thoroughly wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch washes away and the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes to ensure maximum grain elongation.
Using a mortar and pestle, crush the garlic with the turmeric and a pinch of salt. Sauté this paste in a small pan with a drizzle of oil for 3-4 minutes until golden and intensely fragrant.

Drain the meat and chickpeas, reserving 3 cups of the flavorful cooking broth. In a large Dutch oven, layer the drained rice, meat, chickpeas, fried onions, and the toasted garlic-turmeric paste. Toss in the cardamom, coriander, and cloves, sautéing the mixture for 2 minutes to toast the spices.

Pour the reserved broth over the rice. Bring to a vigorous boil until the liquid reduces and small steam holes appear. Drizzle with ghee and the optional 'Golden Touch' of saffron. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel (Dam-koni), seal tightly, and steam on the lowest heat for 45 minutes.
While the rice steams, sauté the pitted dates in a tablespoon of oil for 2 minutes until they become glossy, plump, and slightly caramelized.

Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Plate the aromatic pilaf, topping it with the caramelized dates and a generous dusting of toasted cumin seeds. Serve with fresh Seville orange halves for a bright, citrusy finish.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Eggplant & Beef Rice (Dami Bademjan)
description: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN ONE-POT COMFORT: VELVETY EGGPLANT MEETS SAVORY BASMATI IN A SYMPHONY OF FLAVOR.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a large skillet, sauté the onions in 20g of oil over medium heat until they reach a deep golden hue (Piaz-Dagh). Add the ground beef and turmeric, browning the meat until the fat renders and the aroma is irresistible.

Generously salt the eggplant rounds and let them sit for 20 minutes to sweat out bitterness. Pat dry, then pan-fry both eggplants and potatoes separately in oil until they are beautifully bronzed and semi-tender.
In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, combine the soaked/drained rice, the beef mixture, grated tomatoes, and bell peppers. Season with salt and pepper.

Add enough water to barely cover the rice mixture (about 1.5 cm above the rice). Bring to a vigorous boil over high heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. If using the Saffron Royal Touch, drizzle it over the surface now.

Once the water has mostly evaporated and pits form on the surface, gently place the fried potatoes and eggplants on top of the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to seal the steam.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting and steam for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and a golden crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom. Flip onto a platter to reveal the masterpiece.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Spinach & Cashew Pilaf
description: A VIBRANT FUSION OF EARTHY SPINACH, CRUNCHY CASHEWS, AND WARM SILK ROAD SPICES.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt the butter into the oil over medium heat. Add the onions and sauté for 6-7 minutes until they are soft, translucent, and just beginning to whisper a golden hue.
Stir in the minced garlic and chopped tomatoes. Sauté for another 3 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate, creating a rich base.
Drain the rice and add it to the pot. Sprinkle in the coriander and cumin. Stir gently for 1 minute to toast the grains and coat them in the aromatic spices.

Add the grated carrots and water. Season generously with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.

Lift the lid and quickly layer the fresh spinach and cashews on top of the rice. If using the 'Golden Touch,' drizzle the bloomed saffron over a small section of the rice now. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (damkoni style) to trap the steam, and let it rest on the lowest heat for an additional 10 minutes to wilt the spinach to perfection.
Using a fork, gently fluff the rice to incorporate the vibrant green spinach and crunchy cashews. Transfer to a platter and serve immediately while the aroma fills the room.

english_name: Royal Silk Road Noodle Rice with Black-Eyed Peas
description: A LUXURIOUS SYMPHONY OF TOASTED NOODLES, EARTHY LEGUMES, AND GOLDEN CARAMELIZED ONIONS.

instructions.text: Simmer the soaked black-eyed peas in 3 cups of water for approximately 25-30 minutes until tender to the bite but still holding their shape. Drain and set aside.

In a large pot, bring 8 cups of water with 2 tablespoons of salt to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 5 minutes. Gently stir in the toasted Reshteh noodles and boil for another 2-3 minutes until the rice grains are elongated and soft on the outside but firm at the core.
Drain the rice and noodle mixture into a fine-mesh colander and rinse quickly with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process.

In the same pot, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. Arrange the potato slices at the bottom to create a golden Tahdig. Layer the rice-noodle mixture and the cooked peas, building a pyramid shape. Poke 3 holes through the rice to the bottom to allow steam to circulate.
Cover with a tight lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani). Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes to set the crust, then reduce heat to low and steam for 45 minutes.

While the rice steams, sauté the onions in a pan with the remaining oil and butter until they become deeply caramelized and golden-brown. Stir in the turmeric and black pepper for the last 60 seconds of cooking.

If using the Royal Upgrade, gently sauté the raisins and barberries in a tiny bit of butter for 1 minute until plump. Mix a small portion of the cooked rice with the bloomed saffron water for a vibrant golden contrast.
Platter the fluffy rice, topping it with the caramelized onions, saffron rice, and jeweled fruits. Serve the crispy potato Tahdig on the side.

english_name: Royal Golden Carrot & Meatball Rice (Havij Polo)
description: A RADIANT JEWELED MASTERPIECE OF HONEY-GLAZED CARROTS, FRAGRANT SAFFRON, AND SAVORY SPICED MEATBALLS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté the julienned carrots until they soften and begin to glisten. Dissolve sugar in a 1/4 cup of boiling water and pour over the carrots along with half of the bloomed saffron. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until the liquid reduces to a light syrup and carrots are glazed. Set aside.

In a mixing bowl, combine the ground meat, grated onion, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Knead well for 5 minutes until the mixture becomes tacky. Roll into marble-sized meatballs (Koofteh Ghelgheli). Fry the meatballs in a pan with a touch of oil until golden-brown and crispy on all sides, then gently fold them into the glazed carrot mixture.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Boil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the middle. Drain and rinse quickly with cool water.

In the same pot, heat a splash of oil and water. Place sliced potatoes or lavash bread at the bottom for a legendary Tahdig. Layer the rice and the carrot-meatball mixture into a pyramid shape. Drizzle melted butter and the remaining saffron over the top. Cover with a kitchen towel-wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes until the steam rises and the rice is aromatic.
Flash-fry the slivered pistachios and almonds in butter for 30 seconds until fragrant. Mound the rice on a platter, topping with the crunchy nuts and the golden Tahdig from the bottom of the pot.

english_name: Royal Golden Crust Rice Cake with Savory Eggplant and Lamb
description: A MAJESTIC ARCHITECTURAL MARVEL OF SAFFRON-INFUSED RICE, SILKY EGGPLANT, AND TENDER LAMB WITH A SHATTERING GOLDEN CRUST.

instructions.text: Generously salt the eggplant rounds and let them rest for 20 minutes to sweat out any bitterness. Pat dry with paper towels and fry in hot oil until they develop a deep mahogany-gold color on both sides. Drain on wire racks.

Sauté the diced onions in a heavy-bottomed pan until translucent and golden. Stir in the garlic, turmeric, and meat cubes. Season with salt and pepper, searing the meat for 5 minutes. Add a splash of water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick glaze.

Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of salted boiling water. Boil for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but with a firm bite in the center. Drain and rinse gently with lukewarm water.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks, yogurt, and the bloomed saffron (dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water). This is the 'Golden Binder'. Gently fold the parboiled rice into this mixture until every grain is coated in a vibrant yellow hue.

In a non-stick pot or Dutch oven, add 3 tablespoons of oil. Layer half of the saffron rice, pressing down firmly. Arrange a layer of fried eggplant followed by the tender meat mixture, then top with the remaining rice. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.

Poke several holes through the rice to the bottom using a spoon handle. Distribute butter cubes on top. Cover with a tight-fitting lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam. Cook on medium-low for 60 minutes to develop the legendary crust.

english_name: Aromatic Wild Leek Rice (Valak Polo)
description: A RARE SPRINGTIME TREASURE FEATURING FORAGED WILD LEEKS AND A SHATTERING GOLDEN SAFFRON CRUST.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water several times until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Thoroughly wash the wild leeks, removing any tough stems. Chop them into 1-inch pieces. Their aroma should be reminiscent of mild garlic and spring meadows.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 7-10 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (Al Dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.
In a large bowl, gently fold the chopped wild leeks into the parboiled rice. Season with black pepper to enhance the earthy notes of the greens.
For the Royal Tahdig: In a small bowl, whisk together the yogurt, egg yolks, half of the melted butter, and the bloomed saffron. Mix this with two cups of the rice-leek mixture.
In a non-stick pot, heat a splash of oil. Spread the saffron-yogurt rice mixture evenly across the bottom. Mound the remaining rice on top in a pyramid shape to allow steam to circulate.

Poke a few holes in the rice mound with the handle of a wooden spoon. Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and seal tightly. Cook on medium-high for 10 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to low for 50-80 minutes.
Once finished, pour the remaining melted butter over the rice. Remove from heat and let it rest for 10 minutes before flipping the pot onto a platter to reveal the golden, shatteringly crisp Tahdig.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Herb & Cabbage Rice (Shirazi Kalam Polo)
description: A SYMPHONY OF FRAGRANT HERBS AND GOLDEN MEATBALLS NESTLED IN FLUFFY BASMATI CLOUDS.

instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the ground meat, grated onion, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Knead well for 5 minutes until the mixture becomes tacky, then roll into marble-sized meatballs (Koofteh Ghelgheli).
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Sizzle the meatballs until they are golden-brown and crispy on all sides. Remove and set aside.

In the same skillet, add the shredded cabbage. Sauté for 10-12 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Fold the meatballs back in along with the cinnamon, half the bloomed saffron, and a splash of water. Simmer for 5 minutes until the liquid reduces into a thick glaze.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Parboil the Basmati rice for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but firm in the center. Drain and rinse gently with cool water.

In a clean non-stick pot, heat a layer of oil and the remaining saffron. To create the legendary Tahdig (crispy crust), layer a small amount of rice at the bottom. Begin layering: a thin layer of rice, a handful of fresh herbs (dill, parsley, cilantro, mint), and a portion of the cabbage-meatball mixture. Repeat until all ingredients are used, forming a pyramid shape.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel to trap the steam. Cook on medium-low heat for 45-50 minutes. The aroma of herbs and toasted rice will signal perfection.

english_name: Royal Shirazi Polo: The Jeweled Rice of Shiraz
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN CAKE OF SAFFRON RICE, BURSTING WITH RUBY BARBERRIES AND SILKEN EGGPLANT.

instructions.text: Parboil the washed rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for about 7-10 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but retain a firm bite in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

Prepare the Royal Touch: Bloom the ground saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, egg yolks, half the oil, and 3/4 of the bloomed saffron until a vibrant golden custard forms.

Sauté the eggplant slices in oil until golden brown and tender. Separately, sauté the barberries with sugar in a touch of oil for 1 minute until they puff up like rubies. Set aside some nuts and barberries for the final flourish.

Fold two-thirds of the parboiled rice into the saffron-yogurt mixture. Grease a heavy-bottomed oven-proof pot or glass dish. Spread a thick layer of the golden rice mixture at the bottom, pressing slightly.

Create the layers: Arrange the fried eggplant over the rice, followed by a generous sprinkling of almonds, pistachios, and barberries. Place the pre-cooked meat (braised until tender) on top, then cover everything with the remaining plain white rice.

Drizzle the remaining saffron water and a bit of oil around the edges. Cover tightly with foil and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 90 minutes until the bottom and sides are a deep, shatteringly crisp golden-brown.
Remove from the oven, let it rest for 5 minutes, then carefully invert onto a large platter. Garnish with the reserved nuts and barberries for a 5-star presentation.

english_name: Persian Golden Spinach & Carrot Pilaf (Esfenaj Polo)
description: A VIBRANT TAPESTRY OF EARTHY GREENS, SWEET GOLDEN HARVEST, AND LUXURIOUS CRUNCH.

instructions.text: Heat the sunflower oil and butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Sauté the diced onions until they turn translucent and achieve a soft, golden hue, approximately 7 minutes.
Introduce the crushed garlic and chopped tomatoes to the pot. Sizzle them together for 3 minutes until the tomatoes soften and release their aromatic juices.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Sprinkle in the coriander and cumin powders. Stir gently for 1 minute to toast the grains and coat them in the spiced oils.

Fold in the grated carrots and pour in the water. Season generously with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.

Layer the fresh spinach leaves and cashews across the top of the rice. If using the Saffron Royal Upgrade, drizzle the liquid gold over the surface now. Place a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) under the lid to trap the steam and cook for a final 15-20 minutes until the spinach is wilted and the flavors are fused.
Gently fluff the rice with a fork, mixing the vibrant spinach and crunchy cashews throughout. Serve immediately on a warmed platter.

english_name: Golden Saffron Chicken Tahchin
description: A MAJESTIC GOLDEN SAFFRON RICE CAKE WITH A CRUNCHY CRUST AND TENDER HEART.

instructions.text: Place the chicken breast in a pot with the halved onion, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Cover with water and simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until tender. Once cooled, shred the chicken into succulent bite-sized pieces and set aside.

In a large pot of salted boiling water, parboil the Basmati rice for about 7-8 minutes. The grains should be soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' snap in the middle. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the egg until smooth. Incorporate the yogurt, the bloomed 'Golden Touch' saffron water, turmeric, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. This aromatic emulsion will be the soul of your Tahchin.
Take half of your parboiled rice and gently fold it into the saffron-yogurt mixture until every grain is coated in a vibrant sunrise hue.

Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat with the oil and butter. Once the butter sizzles, spread the saffron-coated rice evenly across the bottom, pressing down firmly with a spatula to create a solid base.

Layer the shredded chicken over the rice base, then cover with the remaining white parboiled rice. Use the back of a spoon to press everything down into a tight, compact cake. Poke a few holes in the rice to allow steam to escape.

Cover the pan tightly (wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel for best results) and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Let it slow-cook for 90 minutes. This patience is rewarded with a majestic, uniform golden crust that crackles when sliced.

english_name: Royal Golden Turmeric Rice with Velvety Fava Beans
description: THE ULTIMATE PERSIAN COMFORT BOWL: RADIANT TURMERIC RICE WITH VELVETY YELLOW FAVA BEANS.

instructions.text: Rinse the yellow fava beans thoroughly. In a heavy-bottomed pot, combine the beans, turmeric, and 3 cups of water. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 15-20 minutes until the beans are tender but still hold their shape.
While the beans simmer, heat oil in a separate pan and sauté the diced onions over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until they reach a deep, translucent gold and release a sweet aroma.

Add the washed Basmati rice, the golden sautéed onions, and salt to the pot with the beans and their remaining cooking liquid. Stir gently once to ensure the turmeric and onions are evenly distributed.
Cook on medium-high heat until the water has mostly evaporated and small steam holes appear on the surface of the rice. If using the Royal Touch, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top now.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (dam-karni), seal tightly, and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Allow the rice to steam for 35 minutes to develop a fluffy texture and a golden crust at the bottom.

english_name: The Jeweled Royal Rice (Javahar Polo)
description: A CULINARY MASTERPIECE OF GOLDEN SAFFRON, VIBRANT JEWELS, AND SUCCULENT CHICKEN FIT FOR A ROYALTY.

instructions.text: Melt half the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté the julienned carrots for 5 minutes until they begin to soften and glisten.
Pour in half of the bloomed saffron (the 'Royal Touch') and 200ml of water. Simmer gently for 15 minutes until the carrots are tender and have absorbed the golden essence.
To remove bitterness from the orange peels, boil them in water for 10 minutes. Drain and repeat this process 3 to 4 times until the aroma is sweet and the bitterness is gone.
Add the prepared orange peels, pistachios, and almonds to the carrot mixture. Sauté for 3 minutes, adding the remaining saffron. Stir well until the 'jewels' are aromatic and vibrant.
In a separate pan, sear the chicken cubes with the remaining butter and salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden-brown and the center is succulent.
Parboil the soaked rice in salted water, drain, and steam in a pot with a tight lid for 30 minutes on low heat to achieve fluffy, individual grains.
In a grand serving platter, layer the fluffy rice with the sweet carrot and nut mixture, lightly sprinkling sugar between the layers for a delicate crystalline finish.
Crown the rice with the golden chicken pieces and garnish with a final flourish of the jeweled mixture.

english_name: Persian Jeweled Rice (Morassa Polo) - The Royal Crown Dish
description: A SYMPHONY OF EDIBLE GEMS AND AROMATIC SAFFRON FIT FOR A MODERN-DAY EMPEROR.

instructions.text: Sauté the diced onions in a heavy-bottomed pot until translucent. Add the chicken pieces, seasoning with salt and pepper. Pour in just enough water to half-cover the chicken, cover, and simmer gently for 45-50 minutes until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.

Prepare the 'Jewels': Boil the orange peels in water for 5 minutes, drain, and repeat three times to remove all bitterness. In the final stage, simmer the peels with 1 cup of water and 0.5 cup of sugar until translucent and syrupy. Drain and set aside.

Wash the rice until the water runs clear. Parboil in a large pot of salted boiling water for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside but firm in the middle. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a clean pot, add a splash of oil and water. Layer half the rice, then place the cooked chicken pieces (bones removed if preferred) in the center. Top with the remaining rice, shaping it into a pyramid. Poke a few holes in the rice to allow steam to escape. Cover with a lid wrapped in a kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to achieve a golden Tahdig crust.

While the rice steams, sauté the barberries and raisins separately in a little oil with a tablespoon of sugar for 2 minutes until they plump up and shine. Flash-fry the almond and pistachio slivers for 1 minute to release their oils—do not brown them.

The Royal Touch: Take 3 tablespoons of the steamed rice and mix with your bloomed saffron liquid. To serve, platter the white rice and chicken, then artistically layer the saffron rice, candied orange peels, barberries, raisins, and nuts in vibrant stripes or patterns.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Herb Rice (Sabzi Polo)
description: A VIBRANT EMERALD FEAST OF FRESH HERBS AND FLUFFY BASMATI, CROWNED WITH GOLDEN SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.
If using lamb, sear the meat in a pot with onions and turmeric, then simmer gently for 90 minutes until the meat is fork-tender. Reserve one ladle of the aromatic broth.
Wash and thoroughly dry the herbs. Finely chop the dill, parsley, cilantro, and chives. Ensuring they are dry before chopping prevents them from turning into a paste.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (Al Dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add 3 tablespoons of oil and a splash of water. Begin layering: a thin layer of rice, followed by a generous handful of mixed herbs. Repeat, building a pyramid shape. Tuck the whole garlic cloves and meat (if using) into the middle layers.

Mix the reserved meat broth (or water) with the remaining oil. Once steam begins to rise from the pot, pour this mixture over the rice. Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Dam-kani) and steam on low heat for 45-60 minutes.
For the finale, take a scoop of the cooked rice and mix it with your bloomed saffron. Crown the platter with this golden rice and a drizzle of hot melted butter for a royal finish.

english_name: Royal Persian Green Bean Rice (Loobia Polo)
description: A CINNAMON-INFUSED MASTERPIECE OF TENDER LAMB AND CRISPY GOLDEN RICE.

instructions.text: Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Sizzle the diced onions until translucent, then add the lamb cubes, black pepper, and cinnamon. Sear the meat until it develops a deep, golden-brown crust and the aroma of cinnamon fills the kitchen.

Stir in the tomato paste and sauté for 2 minutes to unlock its color. Add the green beans and half a cup of water. Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened into a rich, savory coating.

While the meat simmers, wash the Basmati rice until the water runs clear. Bring 2 liters of water with 2 tablespoons of salt to a rolling boil. Add the rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are long and soft on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a clean non-stick pot, melt a small knob of butter. Create the masterpiece by layering: start with a base of white rice, then a generous scoop of the lamb and bean mixture. Repeat the layers, shaping the rice into a pyramid to allow steam to circulate.

Poke 3-4 holes in the rice mound using the back of a spoon. Drizzle with a little water and melted butter. Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap the steam and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until a crispy Tahdig crust forms at the bottom.

For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer of rice. Transfer to a platter, ensuring the meat and rice are gently tossed together, and crown the dish with shards of the crunchy golden Tahdig.

english_name: Persian Adas Polo: The Silk Road Golden Lentil & Jewel Rice
description: A ROYAL SYMPHONY OF EARTHY LENTILS, SWEET SUN-KISSED RAISINS, AND AROMATIC SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice in cold water until the starch runs clear, then soak in salted water for 30 minutes to ensure maximum grain elongation.
In a small pot, simmer the lentils in water until they are 'al dente'—tender but still holding their shape. Drain and set aside.

Sizzle the onions in 2 tablespoons of oil with turmeric over medium heat until they reach a deep, caramelized golden-brown. Stir in the raisins for the final 2 minutes until they plump up like tiny jewels.
Prepare the 'Golden Touch' by dissolving your ground saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water; let it steep to release its royal aroma.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'snap' in the center, then drain.

Layering the masterpiece: Coat the bottom of a non-stick pot with oil. Place a layer of rice, followed by a sprinkle of lentils, the onion-raisin mixture, cinnamon, and pepper. Repeat until a pyramid shape is formed.

Drizzle the saffron infusion and remaining oil over the rice. Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel to trap the steam, and cook on the lowest heat for 40 minutes to develop the legendary crunchy Tahdig crust.

english_name: Royal Golden Shekar Polo
description: A SUN-KISSED SYMPHONY OF SHIRAZI SWEETNESS AND RADIANT SAFFRON GRAINS.

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine 2 cups of sugar with 1.5 cups of water. Simmer over medium heat until the sugar is fully dissolved. For the 'Golden Touch,' stir in the bloomed saffron and set this royal syrup aside to cool.

Bring a large pot of water to a vigorous boil. Add the turmeric for a sun-kissed hue and the coarse salt. Carefully add the pre-soaked rice and boil for 7 to 9 minutes until the grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the center.
Drain the rice into a fine-mesh colander and immediately rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process and wash away excess starch.

Coat the bottom of your pot with half the oil. Gently mound the parboiled rice into the pot in a pyramid shape. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkesh) and steam on low heat for 25 minutes to set the structure of the grains.

Carefully fold half of your saffron syrup into the rice. Return the rice to the pot and drizzle the remaining syrup over the top. Cover and steam for an additional 45 minutes on the lowest possible heat, allowing the sugar to infuse and the bottom to form a sweet crust.

Prepare the citrus garnish: Boil the peel strips in water three times, draining each time to remove bitterness. In a small pan, sauté the peels with 1 tablespoon of sugar and a touch of oil until they are glossy and translucent.
Plate the aromatic rice on a platter, crowning it with the candied citrus peels and vibrant green pistachios for a five-star finish.

english_name: Royal Saffron Tahchin with Golden Crust
description: THE CULINARY CROWN JEWEL: A SHIMMERING GOLDEN RICE CAKE WITH A SHATTERING CRUST AND TENDER SAFFRON-INFUSED HEART.

instructions.text: Place the meat in a pot with turmeric and enough water to cover. Simmer gently for 60 to 90 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and only one cup of concentrated broth remains. Shred the chicken or break the lamb into large, succulent chunks.

In a large bowl, whisk the thick yogurt with the egg yolks, half of the bloomed saffron, salt, and pepper. Fold the cooked meat into this golden mixture and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate the fibers.

Sauté the barberries in butter over medium-low heat. Stir in the sugar, a splash of rosewater, and a teaspoon of saffron water. Cook for 2 minutes until they glisten like rubies, being careful not to burn them.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of salted boiling water until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm snap in the middle (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

Mix three cups of the parboiled rice with a few ladles of the yogurt marinade. Coat the bottom of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot or glass baking dish with half the oil. Spread the yellow rice mixture across the bottom, pressing firmly with a spatula to create the foundation for the crust.

Layer the marinated meat and half the barberries over the rice. Cover with the remaining white rice, pressing down gently. Mix the remaining broth, saffron, and melted butter, then pour it evenly over the top.

Seal the dish tightly with foil or a lid. Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 90 minutes. For a truly thick and legendary 'Tahdig' crust, extend the time by 15 minutes at a lower temperature. Invert onto a platter to reveal the golden masterpiece.

english_name: Royal Saffron-Infused Steamed Chelo
description: THE CROWN JEWEL OF THE PERSIAN TABLE: ETHEREAL, SNOW-WHITE GRAINS WITH A SHATTERING GOLDEN CRUST.

instructions.text: Rinse the rice in a large bowl under lukewarm water, swirling gently and changing the water 5-6 times until it runs crystal clear to remove all surface starch.
Cover the rice with plenty of water and add 2 tablespoons of sea salt. Let it soak for at least 2 hours; this strengthens the grains and allows them to elongate during cooking.
Fill a large non-stick pot with 8 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil. Drain the soaking water from the rice and gently slide the grains into the boiling water.
Parboil the rice for 6 to 8 minutes. Test a grain: it should be soft on the outside but still have a firm, slight 'bite' or white core in the center. Do not overcook.
Drain the rice into a fine-mesh colander and immediately rinse with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process and wash away excess salt.

Clean the pot. Add 2 tablespoons of oil, 1 tablespoon of melted butter, a splash of water, and a drizzle of your bloomed saffron to the bottom of the pot to create the foundation for the golden crust (Tahdig).
Gently layer the rice into the pot, forming a cone shape. Use the handle of a wooden spoon to poke 5-6 holes through the rice mound to the bottom to allow steam to escape evenly.

Cover the pot lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to absorb moisture and place it tightly on the pot. Cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 45 minutes.
Before serving, mix a few spoonfuls of the cooked rice with the remaining bloomed saffron and use it as a 'Golden Touch' garnish over the platter of fluffy white rice.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Milk Rice (Shir Polo)
description: VELVETY BASMATI RICE GENTLY SIMMERED IN CREAMY MILK AND INFUSED WITH THE MAJESTIC AROMA OF PERSIAN SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water several times until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes, then drain thoroughly.

In a large heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, combine the drained rice, 5 cups of milk, 1 cup of water, and sea salt. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon to prevent the milk from scorching or sticking to the bottom.
Once the rice has absorbed most of the liquid and small 'steam holes' appear on the surface, drizzle the bloomed saffron (the Golden Touch) over one side of the rice for a beautiful color contrast.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to seal the steam. Reduce heat to the lowest setting and let the rice steam undisturbed for 25 minutes until the grains are fluffy and elongated.

Cut the butter into small cubes and dot them over the rice. Increase the heat slightly for the final 5 minutes to develop a rich, creamy golden crust (Tahdig) at the bottom. Serve hot with fried raisins and your choice of fish.

english_name: Royal Persian Lentil & Mushroom Rice (Adas Polo)
description: EARTHY LENTILS MEET SAVORY MUSHROOMS IN THIS PROTEIN-PACKED PERSIAN MASTERPIECE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Soak in salted water for at least 30 minutes to ensure long, fluffy grains.
Place lentils in a pot with 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20-25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. Drain any excess liquid.
In a large skillet, sizzle the ground beef with the crispy fried onions until browned. If keeping it vegetarian, skip directly to the mushrooms.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Sear on high heat until they release their moisture and turn a beautiful golden-brown. Stir in turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Add tomato paste to the center of the pan and sauté for 2 minutes until it darkens and smells fragrant. Pour in half a cup of water, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes to create a rich, savory ragu.
Fold the cooked lentils into the mushroom and beef mixture, ensuring every lentil is coated in the aromatic sauce. Set aside.

Boil a large pot of salted water. Parboil the soaked rice for 6-8 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the middle (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a non-stick pot, add a layer of oil. Build the dish by alternating layers of white rice and the lentil-mushroom mixture. Shape into a pyramid and poke holes for steam. Drizzle with remaining oil and the optional bloomed saffron for a royal aroma. Cover with a wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 45 minutes until a crispy Tahdig crust forms.

english_name: Royal Saffron & Barberry Jewel Rice (Zereshk Polo ba Morgh)
description: A SYMPHONY OF RUBY-RED BARBERRIES AND GOLDEN SAFFRON RICE FIT FOR A PERSIAN EMPEROR.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 60 minutes to ensure the grains lengthen beautifully during cooking.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, sear the chicken pieces in oil until golden brown. Add half the sliced onions, garlic, turmeric, cinnamon stick, salt, and pepper. Pour in 2 cups of water, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced to a concentrated nectar.
Debone the chicken if preferred, or keep whole for a rustic presentation. Strain the remaining chicken stock and mix half of it with 1 tablespoon of your bloomed saffron liquid. Keep warm.

Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of boiling salted water for 7-10 minutes until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

To build the 'Tahdig' (crispy bottom), add a splash of oil and saffron water to the pot. Layer the rice and chicken pieces, shaping the rice into a pyramid. Poke holes in the rice to let steam escape, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until a golden crust forms.

While the rice steams, sauté the washed barberries in butter on very low heat for 2 minutes. Add sugar and rosewater, stirring until the berries puff up and shine like rubies. Do not burn them! Mix in the slivered nuts at the final second.

For the grand finale, take a few scoops of the cooked rice and mix with the remaining saffron. Plate the white rice and chicken, then crown it with the golden saffron rice and the glistening jewel-like barberry mixture.

english_name: Aromatic Shirazi Kalam Polow (Cabbage & Herb Rice)
description: THE FRAGRANT JEWEL OF SHIRAZ: CARAMELIZED CABBAGE MEETS AROMATIC HERBS IN A RICE MASTERPIECE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to ensure long, fluffy grains.

In a bowl, combine ground meat, grated onion, salt, and pepper. Knead for 5 minutes until sticky, then roll into marble-sized meatballs (Koofteh Ghelgheli). Lightly dust them with flour and sear in a hot pan with oil until golden-brown and crispy. Set aside.

Sauté the diced onion in a large skillet until translucent. Add the shredded cabbage and turmeric. Sauté over medium heat for 12 minutes until the cabbage is soft, golden, and slightly caramelized. Stir in the Shirazi Advieh and seasoned with salt.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with plenty of salt. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 5-7 minutes. In the final 60 seconds, stir in the fresh chopped herbs. Drain the rice and herbs immediately and rinse with lukewarm water to stop the cooking.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add a splash of oil. Layer the herb-rice with the cabbage mixture and the golden meatballs, stacking them into a pyramid shape. Poke a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape.

Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes until steam builds, then reduce heat to low and steam for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and a crispy Tahdig has formed at the bottom.
For the Royal Upgrade, drizzle your bloomed saffron over the top layer of rice before serving to infuse the dish with a golden glow and floral aroma.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Silk Road Golden Fried Rice
description: A ROYAL SILK ROAD STIR-FRY INFUSED WITH EXOTIC SAFFRON AND TART JEWELED BARBERRIES.

instructions.text: In a large pot, bring 4 cups of salted water to a boil. Add the Basmati rice and parboil for about 8 minutes until the grains are long and 'al dente'—soft on the outside but still firm in the middle.

Drain the rice. In the same pot, add 3 tablespoons of oil, return the rice, and cover with a lid wrapped in a kitchen towel. Steam on the lowest heat for 15-20 minutes to achieve perfectly fluffy, separated grains.
Spread the steamed rice onto a wide tray to cool slightly; this prevents the rice from becoming mushy during the stir-fry phase.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger for 2 minutes until the kitchen is filled with their warm, pungent aroma.
Add the chicken cubes, seasoning with salt and pepper. Sear for 5 minutes until the edges are golden-brown and the meat is tender.
Toss in the bell peppers, corn, and curry powder. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until the vegetables are vibrant and crisp-tender.
Push the ingredients to the side of the pan. Pour the whisked eggs into the center and scramble gently for 1 minute until just set, then fold them into the chicken mixture.

Add the cooled rice to the wok. Drizzle the 'Golden Touch' of bloomed saffron and a dusting of cinnamon over the rice. Toss everything together for 3 minutes on high heat until every grain is coated in color and flavor.

In a small separate pan, quickly sauté the barberries and almonds in butter for 60 seconds until the barberries puff up. Garnish the rice with this royal mixture and serve immediately with a dollop of yogurt.

english_name: Golden Persian Gulf Shrimp & Saffron Rice
description: A ROYAL SEAFOOD SYMPHONY FROM THE PERSIAN GULF, BLENDING SUCCULENT SHRIMP WITH FRAGRANT SAFFRON RICE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 hours to achieve maximum grain length.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with plenty of salt. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water; cook for 6-8 minutes until the grains are 'al dente'—soft on the outside with a firm bite in the middle.

Briefly blanch the cleaned shrimp in boiling water for 90 seconds until they just turn a delicate pink. Drain immediately and shock in cold water to stop the cooking process, ensuring a tender texture.

In a heavy-bottomed skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté the onions for 12-15 minutes until they reach a deep, translucent gold. Stir in the garlic and turmeric, allowing the spices to bloom for 60 seconds.

Add the blanched shrimp to the skillet. Season with salt and pepper, then pour in half of the liquid gold saffron. Sizzle for 2-3 minutes until the shrimp are beautifully coated and infused with the aroma.

Layer the pot: place a layer of parboiled rice at the bottom, followed by a layer of the saffron-shrimp mixture. Repeat until all ingredients are used, shaping the rice into a pyramid. Pour the remaining saffron over the top.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel to trap the steam. Cook on low heat for 35-40 minutes until a crispy crust (Tahdig) forms at the bottom and the rice is fluffy and aromatic.

english_name: Royal Persian Sour Cherry Rice (Albaloo Polo)
description: A VIBRANT CULINARY JEWEL FEATURING RUBY-RED CHERRIES NESTLED IN CLOUDS OF SAFFRON-SCENTED BASMATI.

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan, combine the pitted sour cherries and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat for 10-15 minutes until the cherries release their juices and a light syrup forms. Strain the cherries, reserving the precious ruby syrup for later.

Place chicken in a pot with the onion, a pinch of salt, and enough water to cover. Simmer gently for 25 minutes until tender. Once cooled, shred the chicken into succulent, bite-sized pieces and set aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 7-9 minutes. The grains should be 'Al Dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking.

To build the masterpiece, coat the bottom of a non-stick pot with oil and a splash of the bloomed saffron. Layer one-third of the rice, followed by a layer of shredded chicken and the macerated cherries. Repeat the layers, finishing with a crown of white rice.

Drizzle the reserved cherry syrup and melted butter over the rice mound. Poke a few holes in the rice to allow steam to escape. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel (Damkani) and steam on low heat for 45 minutes to develop a crisp, golden Tahdig crust.
For the grand finale, gently fluff the rice to reveal the stunning pink hues. Garnish with the 'Golden Touch' of remaining saffron rice and a handful of crunchy slivered pistachios and almonds.

english_name: Persian New Year Herb Rice with Crispy Sea Bass (Sabzi Polo ba Mahi)
description: CELEBRATE RENEWAL WITH THE VIBRANT, AROMATIC JEWEL OF PERSIAN CUISINE.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch washes away and the water runs crystal clear. Soak the rice in heavily salted water for at least 4 to 24 hours to ensure the longest, fluffiest grains.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add the soaked rice and parboil for 6-8 minutes. The rice is ready when the outside is soft but the center still has a firm 'bite' (al dente). Drain and rinse gently with lukewarm water.

Thoroughly dry your washed herbs before chopping to prevent them from turning into a paste. In a large bowl, toss the parboiled rice gently with the chopped dill, parsley, cilantro, and fenugreek until the herbs are evenly distributed.

Coat the bottom of a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot with olive oil and a splash of water. Mound the rice-herb mixture into the pot in a pyramid shape, tucking the slivered garlic between the layers. Use the handle of a wooden spoon to poke 3-4 holes in the rice to let steam escape.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni) to trap every drop of steam. Cook on medium-high for 5 minutes to set the crust (Tahdig), then reduce to low and steam for 45-50 minutes until the rice is aromatic and fluffy.

Pat the fish fillets completely dry. Marinate with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. In a hot skillet with olive oil, sear the fish skin-side down for 4-5 minutes until golden-brown and crispy, then flip and cook for 2-3 minutes until the flesh flakes easily with a fork.

For the grand finale, take a scoop of the cooked rice and mix it with your bloomed saffron. Plate the green herb rice, crown it with the golden saffron rice, and serve the crispy fish alongside with fresh lemon wedges.

english_name: Royal Saffron Baghali Polo (Persian Dill & Fava Bean Rice)
description: THE EMERALD JEWEL OF PERSIAN CUISINE: A FRAGRANT CLOUD OF DILL AND CREAMY FAVA BEANS CROWNED WITH ROYAL SAFFRON.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice repeatedly until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least 2 to 3 hours to ensure maximum grain length.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 2 tablespoons of salt and the ground turmeric to give the rice a subtle golden undertone.

Add the drained rice and the peeled fava beans to the boiling water. Let them dance in the water for 5-7 minutes until the rice grains are tender on the outside but still have a firm 'bite' in the center.
One minute before draining, gently fold in the finely chopped fresh dill. Drain the mixture into a fine-mesh colander and rinse with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process.
Prepare the pot for the 'Tahdig' by adding oil and 1/4 cup of water to the bottom. Layer the rice and bean mixture into the pot, forming a pyramid shape to allow steam to circulate freely.

Poke several holes in the rice mound with the handle of a wooden spoon. Cover with a lid wrapped in a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) and cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes until steam forms, then reduce to low and steam for 45 minutes.

For the Royal Finish: Melt butter with a splash of hot water or chicken stock and drizzle over the rice. Take a bowl of the top rice, mix with your bloomed saffron, and use it to garnish the platter before serving.

english_name: Persian Silk-Velvet Kateh
description: EXPERIENCE THE CLOUD-LIKE PERFECTION OF NORTHERN IRAN'S SIGNATURE ONE-POT RICE.

instructions.text: Place the rice in a large bowl and rinse gently with cool water, swirling with your fingers. Repeat 3-4 times until the water runs crystal clear, then drain completely.
In a heavy-bottomed non-stick pot, combine the rinsed rice, 5 cups of filtered water, sea salt, and the butter. If using the Golden Touch, stir in your bloomed saffron now for a royal amber hue.
Bring the mixture to a rapid boil over high heat. Stir once or twice to ensure the salt is dissolved and the butter is beautifully melted and coating the grains.
Allow the water to evaporate until small 'steam craters' form on the surface of the rice. Once the liquid is level with the grains, reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (the traditional Damkani) to trap every drop of aromatic steam. Cover tightly and let the rice rest and steam undisturbed for 30 minutes until the grains are long, fluffy, and tender.

english_name: Southern Coast Aromatic Shrimp & Golden Egg Rice
description: A LUXURIOUS COASTAL TREASURE FEATURING TENDER SHRIMP AND PILLOWY GOLDEN EGGS EMBEDDED IN AROMATIC STEAMED BASMATI.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under lukewarm water until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water for at least 1 hour to ensure maximum grain elongation.
Parboil the rice in a large pot of boiling salted water. Drain when the grains are soft on the outside but still retain a firm 'bite' in the center (Al Dente). Set aside.
In a large skillet, sauté the minced garlic and fried onions in 3 tablespoons of oil until the aroma fills your kitchen and the garlic is pale gold.

Whisk the eggs vigorously in a bowl. Pour them into the skillet with the garlic and onions. Lower the heat, cover the pan, and allow the eggs to steam and set into a soft, fluffy omelet-like consistency.

Briefly poach the shrimp in simmering water for 2 minutes until just pink. Drain and fold them into the egg mixture. Stir in the tomato paste (dissolved in 2 tablespoons of warm water), salt, and pepper until the mixture is beautifully crimson and well-combined.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add a layer of oil. Begin layering the rice and the shrimp-egg mixture, starting and ending with rice to create a mountain shape. If using, drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top layer for a Royal Upgrade. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, seal the pot, and steam on low heat until the rice is perfectly fluffy and a golden crust forms at the bottom.

While the rice steams, blanch the tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds, peel the skins, and dice them. Sauté the tomatoes in 2 tablespoons of oil until they soften into a thick, jammy consistency. Season with a pinch of salt.
To serve, platter the aromatic rice, making sure to showcase the shrimp and egg layers, then crown the dish with the sautéed jammy tomatoes.

english_name: Shiraz-Style Aromatic Kohlrabi & Lentil Yakhni
description: A RUSTIC CULINARY MASTERPIECE: HEARTY LENTILS AND VELVETY KOHLRABI SLOW-COOKED TO PERFECTION.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the oil over medium heat and sauté the onions until they turn translucent and take on a soft golden hue.

Add the meat chunks to the pot, searing them until browned on all sides to lock in the juices. Stir in the turmeric and black pepper, allowing the spices to bloom in the oil for 60 seconds until fragrant.
Incorporate the tomato paste, stirring constantly for 2 minutes until it deepens in color and loses its raw metallic edge.

Add the prepared kohlrabi cubes and the soaked lentils. Pour in the water, ensuring all ingredients are submerged. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to a low simmer, covering the pot tightly.
Simmer gently for about 90 minutes. At this halfway point, add the pierced dried limes and salt. The limes will impart a signature citrusy depth without overpowering the lentils.

Continue cooking for another 30-45 minutes until the meat is falling off the bone and the lentils are butter-soft. If using the Royal Upgrade, stir in the bloomed saffron now for a golden aromatic finish.

The traditional serving ritual: Carefully strain the broth into a separate bowl—this liquid gold is used for 'Tilit' (soaking flatbread). Extract the limes and squeeze their concentrated juice back into the solids.
Remove any bones from the meat. Using a heavy masher, crush the meat, kohlrabi, and lentils together into a rich, rustic paste. Serve the mash and broth side-by-side.

english_name: Royal Jewel Rice with Caramelized Lentils and Golden Zest
description: A SYMPHONY OF SWEET AND SAVORY FEATURING GOLDEN ZEST AND EARTHY LENTILS.

instructions.text: Prepare the citrus zest by boiling the julienned orange strips in water for 5 minutes. Drain and repeat for another 10 minutes to completely remove bitterness, ensuring a delicate floral aroma.

In a small saucepan, simmer the softened zest with sugar or honey and 2 tablespoons of water until a light syrup forms. Toss in the almonds and pistachios for 2 minutes to glaze them, then strain and set aside.

Boil the lentils in salted water for 15-18 minutes until tender but still holding their shape (al dente). In a separate pan, sizzle the raisins in a tablespoon of butter for 60 seconds until they plump up beautifully.
Parboil the Basmati rice in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water until the grains are soft on the outside but firm in the center. Drain and rinse with lukewarm water.

Layer the pot: start with a base of oil and rice, then alternate layers of rice and the lentil-onion-raisin mixture. Shape into a pyramid, poke holes for steam, and cook on low heat with a wrapped lid for 45 minutes to achieve a perfect steam.
Before serving, drizzle the 'Golden Touch' bloomed saffron and melted butter over the fluffy rice. Garnish generously with the glazed citrus zest and nuts.

english_name: Velvety Persian Rice Pudding with Grape Molasses
description: A GOLDEN, EARTHY MASTERPIECE INFUSED WITH THE DEPTH OF ANCIENT VINE MOLASSES.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot, whisk together the milk, sugar, and vanilla. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat until the sugar is fully dissolved.

Fold the soaked rice and grape molasses into the milk. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, for about 40 minutes or until the rice is completely tender and the mixture has thickened to a creamy consistency.
Stir in the butter and freshly grated nutmeg. If using the 'Royal Upgrade,' fold in your saffron-rosewater infusion now to elevate the aroma to a palace-worthy level.

Pour the mixture into a glass Pyrex or ceramic baking dish. Place in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F) and bake for 60 minutes. Look for a beautiful, golden-brown caramelized skin to form on the surface.
Allow the pudding to set for at least 15 minutes. Serve warm for a comforting hug or chilled for a refined treat, garnished with a dollop of tart sour cherry or blackberry jam.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Gulf Shrimp Rice (Meygoo Polo)
description: A SYMPHONY OF SOUTHERN PERSIAN SPICES AND SUCCULENT SHRIMP NESTLED IN HERB-INFUSED RICE.

instructions.text: Sauté one diced onion in a large skillet with a splash of oil until translucent. Add the cleaned shrimp and sauté over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes until they turn pink and the moisture evaporates. Avoid overcooking to keep them succulent.
Dust the shrimp with the ground cinnamon, stirring for 30 seconds to allow the warm aroma to neutralize the sea scent. Remove from the skillet and set aside.

In the same skillet, add the second diced onion and sauté until golden brown. Stir in the fresh herb mix (coriander, fenugreek, and dill) and fry them for about 5-7 minutes until they darken and become intensely fragrant.
Add the minced garlic, turmeric, black pepper, and Persian Advieh to the herbs. Return the shrimp to the pan, season with sea salt, and toss everything together for 2 minutes to marry the flavors.
Parboil the soaked rice in a large pot of boiling salted water until the grains are soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the center. Drain and rinse with cool water.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, add a layer of oil. Begin layering: a few spatulas of parboiled rice, a sprinkle of dried dill, and a generous portion of the shrimp-herb mixture. Repeat until all ingredients are used, forming a pyramid shape.

Optional Golden Touch: Drizzle your bloomed saffron water over the top layer for a royal finish. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (Damkoni), seal tightly, and steam on low heat until the rice is fluffy and a crispy Tahdig has formed at the bottom.

english_name: Royal Saffron Milk Rice
description: THE GOLDEN SILK OF PERSIAN DESSERTS CAPTURED IN EVERY AROMATIC SPOONFUL.

instructions.text: Begin by rinsing the rice under cold water until the starch washes away and the water runs clear. Soak the rice in fresh water for at least 60 minutes to ensure the grains expand and soften beautifully during cooking.

Drain the rice and place it in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add the milk, sugar, cloves, and crushed cardamom pods. Bring the mixture to a very gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally to prevent the milk from scorching on the bottom.

Once the milk begins to steam, pour in your 'Golden Touch'—the bloomed saffron—along with the raisins. Lower the heat to the minimum and cover the pot. Allow it to simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until the rice has fully absorbed the aromatic milk and turned a deep, royal gold.
Drizzle the melted butter over the rice and fold it in with a silicone spatula using a gentle lifting motion to avoid breaking the delicate grains. This adds a five-star velvet sheen to the dish.

Transfer the rice to a decorative serving platter. Remove the whole cloves and cardamom pods if desired. Garnish with a vibrant emerald dust of pistachio powder and serve while the aroma fills the room.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Vegetable Pilau
description: VIBRANT, JEWELED GRAINS INFUSED WITH ANCIENT SPICES AND GARDEN-FRESH VEGETABLES.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water multiple times until the water runs crystal clear to remove excess starch. Combine rice and vegetable broth in a pot, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 12-15 minutes until the liquid is fully absorbed and the grains are fluffy.
In a wide, heavy-bottomed skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until they release their earthy aroma.
Add the chopped onions to the skillet. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until they reach a deep golden-brown caramelization.
Toss in the bell peppers, carrots, and peas. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until the vegetables are tender yet retain a slight 'al dente' crunch and vibrant color.
Stir in the turmeric, salt, and black pepper. If using the 'Royal Touch,' drizzle the bloomed saffron over the vegetable mixture now to infuse the oil with a golden hue.
Gently fold the cooked rice into the vegetable medley using a silicone spatula, being careful not to break the long grains. Allow them to cook together for 2-3 minutes to marry the flavors.
Transfer to a warm serving platter and garnish generously with hand-torn cilantro and mint for a burst of herbal freshness.

english_name: Silk Road Golden Fusion Rice
description: A LUXURIOUS FUSION OF CRUNCHY CASHEWS, SILKY CHEESE, AND AROMATIC BASMATI GEMS.

instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice under cold water until the starch runs clear. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes, then parboil in a large pot of bubbling water for 7-9 minutes until the grains are 'Al Dente'—firm in the center but soft on the outside. Drain and steam with a damp cloth under the lid for 30-40 minutes until fluffy.
While the rice steams, place the cubed curd cheese in a small bowl and toss with the 4 tablespoons of soy sauce. Let it marinate for at least 15 minutes to absorb that rich umami flavor.

Heat oil in a large wok or skillet. Sauté the onions until translucent and fragrant. Add the diced carrots and bell peppers, stir-frying over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until the edges are slightly caramelized and tender-crisp.
In a separate pan, sear the mushrooms on high heat until they release their moisture and turn a deep golden brown. Toss in the green peas and toasted cashews for the last 2 minutes to warm through.

Gently fold the sautéed vegetables, mushrooms, cashews, and the marinated cheese (including the soy sauce) into the fluffy white rice. If you desire a 'Royal Upgrade,' drizzle your bloomed saffron over a small portion of the rice before mixing for a stunning golden contrast.

For a 5-star presentation, lightly grease a ring mold or bowl. Pack the rice mixture firmly into the mold, then carefully invert it onto a pre-warmed serving platter. Serve immediately while the aromas are at their peak.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Royal Golden Barberry Rice
description: A MAJESTIC SYMPHONY OF RUBY-RED BARBERRIES AND GOLDEN SAFFRON RICE HIDING TENDER TREASURES OF POACHED CHICKEN.

instructions.text: Wash the rice repeatedly until the water runs clear. Soak in salted water with a pinch of saffron for 30 minutes to strengthen the grains and infuse a base aroma.
Place the chicken and quartered onion in a pot. Season with salt and pepper, add just enough water to cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.

Remove the chicken from the broth, discard the bones, and shred the meat into bite-sized chunks. Bloom your remaining saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water (or over ice) to unlock the Royal Golden Touch.

Drain the rice. In a non-stick pot, bring fresh water to a boil, add the rice, and cook for 6-8 minutes until the exterior is soft but the core is still firm (al dente). Drain and rinse with cool water.

Add oil and a splash of saffron water to the bottom of the non-stick pot. Layer half the rice, then place the shredded chicken in the center, and cover with the remaining rice. Poke holes in the rice to let steam escape, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 40 minutes.
While the rice steams, melt butter in a small pan. Sauté the barberries with sugar on low heat for only 2 minutes until they glisten like rubies. Do not overcook as they burn easily.
Carefully invert the pot onto a large platter to reveal the golden Tahdig crust. Garnish generously with the sautéed barberries and a final drizzle of saffron butter.

english_name: Chef Zaffaron's Golden Aromatic Rice Croquettes
description: CRISPY ON THE OUTSIDE, MELTY ON THE INSIDE: THE ULTIMATE GOLDEN TREASURE BITE.

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled rice with the minced aromatic herbs, salt, pepper, and the bloomed saffron. Gradually incorporate the beaten eggs, mixing thoroughly until the rice becomes a moldable, fragrant dough.

Take a walnut-sized portion of the rice mixture and flatten it in your palm. Place a pinch of mozzarella in the center, then gently fold the rice over to hide the 'treasure,' rolling it into a perfectly smooth sphere.
Dredge each rice ball lightly in a shallow bowl of Panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to ensure an even, textured coat that will shatter upon the first bite.

Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Carefully lower the croquettes into the hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, rotating occasionally, until they achieve a deep, regal golden-brown hue and a crispy exterior.

english_name: Golden Crust Royal Persian Chelou
description: EXPERIENCE THE MAJESTY OF IRAN WITH INDIVIDUAL SNOW-WHITE GRAINS AND A SHATTERING GOLDEN SAFFRON CRUST.

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash the rice in a large bowl, changing the water 5-6 times until the water remains crystal clear to remove all excess surface starch.

Fill a large pot with water and bring to a rolling boil. Add the sea salt. Once boiling, add the washed rice and parboil for 7 to 10 minutes. The grains should be soft on the outside but still have a firm 'al dente' bite in the center.
Drain the rice into a fine-mesh colander and immediately rinse with lukewarm water to stop the cooking process and wash away any residual saltiness.

In a separate bowl, prepare the 'Golden Touch' (Tahdig mixture) by whisking the yogurt, egg yolks, half of the oil, and the ground saffron (bloomed in 2 tablespoons of hot water). Fold in two large spatulas of the parboiled rice until fully coated.
In a non-stick pot, heat the remaining oil with a splash of water. Spread the saffron-yogurt rice mixture evenly across the bottom, pressing down slightly to create a uniform base.
Gently mound the remaining white rice over the base in the shape of a pyramid. Using the handle of a wooden spoon, poke 5 holes into the rice mound to allow steam to escape.

Wrap the pot lid in a clean kitchen towel (Dam-koni) to trap moisture. Cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes until steam begins to form, then reduce to the lowest possible setting and steam for 60 to 90 minutes to develop the golden crust.
Remove from heat and place the bottom of the pot on a cold, damp towel for 2 minutes. This shock helps release the Tahdig perfectly before flipping onto a serving platter.

english_name: Aromatic Persian Mung Bean Rice (Mash Polo)
description: THE EARTHY NUTTINESS OF ANCIENT GRAINS MEETS THE SWEET CARAMEL OF PERSIAN ONIONS IN EVERY FLUFFY BITE.

instructions.text: Wash the Basmati rice in cold water until the starch clears. Soak in heavily salted water for 45 minutes to strengthen the grain structure.
In a dry skillet, toast the mung beans over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until they release a nutty fragrance. Be careful not to burn them.
Place the toasted beans in a pot with 2.5 cups of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15-20 minutes until parboiled—they should be tender but still hold their shape.
In a separate wide pot, sauté the onions in oil until they reach a deep, glistening caramel gold. Stir in the turmeric and black pepper for 60 seconds to wake up the oils.
Drain the soaked rice. Add it to the pot with the mung beans (and their remaining liquid). Gently fold in the caramelized onions, raisins, and cinnamon if using.
Cover the lid with a clean kitchen towel (Damkani) to trap steam. Cook on medium-high for 3 minutes to set the crust, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 35 minutes.
Drizzle with saffron water for a 'Royal Touch' and let it rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork and serving.

english_name: Aromatic Silk Road Lamb Pilaf
description: A REGAL TAPESTRY OF TENDER LAMB, CRUNCHY ALMONDS, AND JEWELED FRUITS FROM THE HEART OF PERSIA.

instructions.text: In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the lamb fat or ghee over medium-high heat until it sizzles. Add the lamb cubes in a single layer, searing them for 6-8 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms on all sides. Remove the meat and set aside, leaving the flavorful drippings in the pot.

Lower the heat to medium and add the sliced onions to the pot. Sauté slowly for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they transform into a soft, translucent amber gold. This is the foundation of our flavor.

Add the crushed almonds and the drained rice to the onions. Stir constantly for 5 minutes to toast the rice grains and nuts in the fat; this ensures the rice remains fluffy and individual rather than mushy.

Stir in the sugar, black pepper, cayenne, and Advieh spices. Pour in the 4 cups of broth and add the raisins. Bring to a gentle boil, then immediately reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer for 20 minutes until the liquid is fully absorbed by the aromatic rice.

Gently fold the seared lamb, chopped parsley, and sage into the rice. If using the 'Royal Upgrade', drizzle the bloomed saffron over the top now. Cover with a clean kitchen towel under the lid and let the dish rest off the heat for 20 minutes to allow the steam to finish the lamb and the flavors to harmonize perfectly.

english_name: Persian Three-Color Jewel Rice (Polo Se Rang)
description: A VIBRANT TRI-COLOR MASTERPIECE CAPTURING THE LUXURY OF THE SILK ROAD IN EVERY GRAIN.
